text: I started taking my car here when I first moved to the area, about 2 and a half years ago. I'll admit I was lured in by the coupons I get in the mail that advertise an oil change for $20. This also includes changing the oil filter, and a look at the brakes, among other things. Frankly, it costs more for me to change my oil myself than to have them do it, so I let them. I went to this Midas 4 times between 2010 and early 2012, and never had a problem. Then I went again this week. I dont know if there was a change in management or what, but it was quite different this time. I found the manager or the person who dealt with the customers to be infuriating. He lied to me and his poor grasp of the English language (he's American, born and raised, BTW) was maddening. First, the oil change. My car takes 7 quarts of oil. The coupon I used (and have used in the past) specifies that it is good for up to 5 quarts. Despite this, I had never been charged for additional oil in the past; this guy tried to charge me. More than that, he also tried to charge me more for my oil filter because it wasnt the kind they typically use or some such nonsense (they had never tried to charge me extra for this before). When he first told me this, the additional charge for the filter was $9. As he continued to talk, it went up to $11 and then to $13 or $14. I protested the increased cost and he showed me on his computer where I had "paid" in the upper 30s for this work in the past. I dont know where this came from though, as I looked at my credit card statements from previous trips to Midas for an oil change and the charges are clearly $20 plus tax. I could see this wasnt going to be good, so I changed the conversation to another problem with the car. After agreeing to get other things fixed on the car, he told me he'd do the oil change for free. Yet, I was somehow charged $20 for it. After getting my car up on a jack, he told me that I needed a new tire. He showed me that my tire's steel belts were showing, so this was a legitimate problem. Honestly, I dont know how I hadnt had a blowout up to that point. I asked if they had a tire. They said yes, but it was one I'd never heard of. He told me they could get another one though. I asked if they could get it that day and have it installed that day and he said yes. As we looked through his list of what others were available, he changed his mind and told me he would not be able to get the tire and install it same day. So I got the one he had in stock. When he went to change the tire, he kept saying how one of the lug nuts was going to break. They he would continue by saying if it breaks. Which is it? Is it going to break or is there only a chance of it breaking? He just could not wrap his head around this concept. In the end, the part that was "going to break" didnt. Makes me wonder if they know what they're doing. The third problem I had was the biggest: the brakes. Two times ago when I brought the car in, about 10,000 miles ago, I asked how the brakes were (remember, brake check is included with oil change package). They told me they were ok, and that I could get another 10,000 miles out of them. The last time I came in, I asked again, and they said the brakes were fine. So this time, I expected the brakes just about needed to be changed, so I told them to look at them. They did and told me the brakes were shot, needed to be replaced, and that since I'd been riding with them like this for so long, I needed new rotors too. I was really upset with this, because if they had done their job in telling how the brakes were previously, this wouldnt have been an issue - I could have had them replaced last time without replacing the rotors ($180 for the pair). I can tell you the brakes were no worse now than they were last time I took the car in. So to sum up, their incompetence/negligence cost me about $200 due to the issue with the rotors. They also charged me an extra $50 for a brake sensor (I could have told them not to, but wanted to prevent this in the future, so I let them), but after I got the car back, the sensor didnt work. For all this, I had to sit in the hot waiting room for 4 hours plus on a 100 degree day. The initial estimate they gave me for all this work was around $340, but it ended up being $560, and that was with a coupon. The manager/customer service guy seems to have forgotten to add in labor to the estimate. I dont know if it was just this one guy, or a change in policy or if some of the people there just dont know what they're doing, but I will never take my car here again.

text: That will be my one and only time at the Hotel Preston!! I stayed here last weekend and was very disappointed. Upon arriving at the hotel I was greeted to a lobby that was under repair...Once I checked in it only got worse. The originally gave me a room that was right in front of the elevator....who wants to stay there? The front desk was helpful in getting me a new room but it didn't get much better. My floor was designated on as a non smoking floor but it sure didn't smell like it. Later that night I had to go down a floor to get ice and found the issue; the stair wells are used as smoking area and cigarette butts are everywhere!!! DISGUSTING!!! I even took pictures to send to the hotel. The hotel itself looks like someone took an old holiday inn and tried to renovate it into a trendy hotel but ran out of money. If you actually look at the quality of the hotel everything looks like it was just slapped together. The walls/doors are paper thin and you can hear everything. And what is going on with the elevator walls?!?! Looks to be a cow hide that was dyed red and had patches removed.... The rooms look fairly nice but the beds are uncomfortable and you are only full size beds in the rooms with two beds, for a 3.5 star hotel this just isn't okay. The bathroom sink area looks nice but the shower looks to have the original white tile that wasn't renovated with the rest of the hotel. Where is the fan in the bathrooms? I had to shower with the door open just so I could breath in there... The hotel offers a shuttle but beware its $18.00 to go downtown!! Its cheaper to drive yourself and park and much more convenient. We didn't figure this out until after we got in the van and were told by the other couple in there A 3.5 star hotel this is not!! The only way I can see them getting that rating is based on the amenities they offer...wanna rent a Ferrari? They can provide that but forget to the small things like replacing the shampoo/soap when they clean your room. I Just can't recommend this hotel to anyone unless your just looking for a bed to sleep in....

text: Sorry for the lapse in writing...work and a trip have gotten me behind in my writing....but I digress.... On May 13th, we ventured to the Continental Treat to which we haven't been since we moved here in 2003. As always, I love the location and how the windows just open up the restaurant. There are two areas, one is the restaurant and the other has a bar to which we didn't go...MAYBE next time. However, onward and forward with the dinner we go.... We were seated quickly as we had reservations, though I am unsure as to needing them since the restaurant seems to be a "neighbourhood" spot and the background of the people seems to be more Northern European to begin with who more than likely enjoy hearty and solid food, which is what you will get here. On this night, I ordered the "special" since the "Beef Stroganoff" was featured and my companion ordered the Rainbow Trout. Before I go any further however, I should mention that on the website they mention that they have a "Vegetarian" Menu (which we weren't given) and they do have a wine list (another thing we weren't given) until the waitress came and we had our questions about the menu. Now, the Vegetarian menu I get not bringing straight away, but the Wine List? Our waitress was very cheerful and chatted with us when she came to the table...wait, wait, I didn't tell you that we ordered an appetizer, did I? Well, we did....it was forgotten until we mentioned it and for the entire dinner time (and even when we left) we were offered the appetizer anyway or to get "to go" since it is "amazing"....we had ordered the "Homemade Perogies". In truth, the waitress was apologetic, so I won't be sarcastic anymore ;-] Instead, I'll tell you about my BEEF Stroganoff....I say it in this way because, unfortunately, I was SO looking forward to having it: Beef, mushrooms and homemade spaetzle...anyone who knows me knows I am putty in their hands with homemade noodles and saucy beef. Tonight was not the night for me....it was more Mushroom Stroganoff, which had a wonderful flavour and the spaetzle was really well made. The salad that came with the feature dinner was quite nice. My companion's trout on the other hand was very good and very well prepared....tasted like lake trout :-] and it was crisp on the outside and tender on the inside. Oh, yes, we did order wine...well, champagne...they have the Henkel which is commonly referred to as " Mrs.'s " Champagne since they had a regular customer for many years who would start with one spit and then order a second....it was a cute story actually as told by our waitress. I have to say, my dessert was MUCH more appealing than my companion's, though his had such a description that when he got it, he was quite disappointed: the Torte....trust me, you don't want to order it....it sounded like it was to be a huge cake and then, it is a simple layer cake... Mine, on the other hand was quite good...the "Picrnik"...an apple spice cake which was moist and tasty (Not to be confused with the apple spice cake I had at the Wildflower Restaurant--hard as a rock). In all, we had a pleasant evening....however, if I return, I will order something else since having read some other reviews of CT, we should give it another shot...but for now, my opinion is what it is....okay in a serious pinch, but not on my top 5 list....

text: We had a surprisingly good time at Bistro St. Tropez - I had not been for a few years and vaguely remembered it being decent but not especially memorable. We trudged our way through the design center, merrily window shopping along the way and arrived on the top floor where this restaurant is located. The wait staff went in a few directions - most of them were very efficient, quietly removing plates and refilling water in a formal manner, keeping their eyes downcast as if someone in the kitchen was waiting to hit them with a giant baguette if they dared to look a customer in the eye. Our main waitress Emma was a delight- charming and funny and she really added to our enjoyment of the meal. The décor seems to go in a few directions as well - part of the dining room is on the formal side with upholstered chairs, another section has fun, modish red chairs and various colored spot lights - I guess trying to create the South of France look. Another area has barstools up against a shelf that look out to the city and hubby mentioned it might be nice to sit there and have a drink and I agreed. There is a great view from the restaurant, maybe not the best angle to view the city from but it's nice to look out at all the sparklling lights. We went for the "Degustation Menu" of three courses for $28 which included a Starter, Main Course and Dessert. I started with a glass of Provencal rosé and was happy to discover it actually tasted like the rosés commonly served in Provence - dry and earthy with flecks of sunshine in it. Hubbies chilled cucumber melon soup had a surprising but delicious tomato base and was a sort of tasty gourmet gazpacho with chunky veggies. My roasted corn soup was very nice- smooth and creamy with a little sweetness from the apple and just a hint of smoke. A basket of fresh rolls with an enjoyable pesto/olive oil dip was served with the soup. Our entrees were mostly excellent - his scallops were perfectly cooked, sweet and nicely seared and he loved the eggplant "caviar" served along with it. Though I couldn't taste the "pistachio goat cheese crust" that was described on the menu my salmon and asparagus wrapped in phyllo was juicy and rich and very good. The ratatouille served with it was excellent; the grayish cauliflower puree was not since it was rather unappetizing, both visually and gustatorily (is that a word??). I choose the profiteroles for dessert and hubby had the praline mousse with a roasted peach. The choux pastry puffs filled with vanilla ice cream and drizzled with a thick chocolate sauce were good but honestly I like the way I make them better, these were a bit dry (whereas the ones I make are buttery and tender - no doubt mine are the incorrect way though!). His dessert was brought out with a smoking lavender frond to flavor the peach and it did that splendidly - the mousse was rich and wonderful. Between the wait staff, the décor etc I just had the sense that the restaurant has a bit of an identity crisis - is it formal or fun? Paris or the Mediterranean coast in summer? Their menu and service comes across as "Fine Dining" yet they have a wine club (buy 10 bottles, get one free) on their website - hmmm, I don't know. I do know we had a great night out - the three course menu was a good value and liquor was reasonable as well. It was nice to eat lovely food while looking out to the city lights.

text: Everyone raves about the great Vin de Set, and we were excited to try! People rave about the view of downtown, we were excited to view! So, we arrived and were promptly seated at a great table along the railing...looking out over a truncated view of the arch and some warehouse and a parking lot...great view? Maybe I was supposed to be just looking up and enjoying being outside? No idea. No view. I get a better view of downtown on my commute down 40/64 every day. Moving on: the food. For starters we had fried oysters and muscles/clams. Both of these items might have been fantastic, but they used so much spice on both of them, it was hard to taste the actual food. I felt like my taste buds were fried by the first bite and all I got after that was texture....but, on a positive note, the texture wasn't bad. Next up, the main course - lobster pot-pie and tuna! So much hope! First, the tuna -- the tuna should not have been cooked first and then placed under a heating element to wait for the lobster to be finished cooking. Guess what, searing a tuna steak does not take that much time, first day in the kitchen? Yes, the glaze on top of the tuna was nice, and pretty tasty, but there isn't enough glaze in the world to rehydrate a very dry chunk of tuna. The lobster pot pie you ask? Well, here is a hint to chef - Lobster pot pie is not puff pastry placed on top of a bowl of lobster bisque. Seriously...where is the pot? I've had some AWESOME lobster pot pies in my time, but this one = blah. Also, quick question, does Vin de Set buy special lobsters that don't have tails or full claws? I only ask because I've never seen a lobster dish that had less lobster. I felt like we sure paid for the full lobster, but only part arrived. The full extent of the lobster in the dish was two pieces of claw meat...not the full claw meat, just the big part of the pincher. I love tail meat, wtf?! Where is my tail?! Maybe they were serving lobster salad at one of three weddings having receptions that night...talk about a place I would never want to have a party...much less a meal again. Lastly, dessert. In my opinion, a good dessert can salvage any meal, no matter how bad. However, in this case, there wasn't even anything on the menu that was worth trying. But, speaking of trying, this menu was REALLY trying, as in contrived. Why can't a place just cook the food correctly, rather than trying to make it all cutting edge? The harder you try, the harder you fail. Also, with a name like Vin de Set, shouldn't there be some kind of French flair...somewhere? And no, New Orleans dishes don't count as French. I really want to give them 1 star, but everyone was nice and we got seated quickly....so, that is worth an extra star. But believe me, it wasn't for the food.

text: I have curly hair and I came here for a Deva-style cut, which consists of cutting your curls while the hair is dry so as to maintain your curl pattern and spring. "Disappointed" doesn't even begin to describe my experience here. After reading the forums on naturallycurly.com and seeing the astounding before and after pictures on the DevaCurl website, I had high expectations that my curls would look fabulous after a proper Deva cut. But seeing my hair after I walked out of this place, I couldn't have made my hair look any frizzier, drier and stickier if I tried! Thankfully, the cut itself was fine (although I have been assured by friends who have had proper Deva cuts in the past that what I received was NOT a deva cut). Had my hair been properly styled, I probably would have walked out a happy customer. I'm sure their stylist took the Deva course (otherwise she wouldn't have been listed on the DevaCurl website), but it's clear that she had no clue how to handle mine. First of all, she practically rushed me right to the sink to have my hair washed after she sat me down for barely 5 minutes to run her fingers through my hair and ask me how I wanted it cut. She didn't take the time to examine my curl pattern or hair properties to really understand how to properly handle it. During the wash, she didn't volunteer any information as to what she was using on my hair or how she was washing and applying product. I had to ask questions if I wanted to get any sort of info. She then rushed me to the hood dryer and sat me down in it for about 20 mins. When she came back, I told her that my hair wasn't dry yet, but she said, "oh it's ok if it's still a little damp". She then proceeded to cut my hair, all the while running her fingers through my hair endlessly and raking out whatever frizz-free curls were attempting to form themselves. My hair was a matted, frizzy mess after a few minutes. She then started to spritz it with water from time to time in an attempt to keep the frizz at bay, and kept slathering on pomade. After the cut was finished, she offered to rinse my hair again because "I touched it so much it caused a little frizz". She ended up shampooing and conditioning it all over again and half-heartedly scrunched in some unknown product to it. She then proceeded to dry it with a terry-cloth towel. One of the 10 commandments of curl care is to NEVER use a terry-cloth towel in your hair. You should use something with a completely flat surface to gently scrunch your curls because the raised fibers in towels disturb the cuticle and cause frizz. All the girls I know that have had Deva cuts have had it scrunched with paper towels. I was in complete shock. Had I been braver, I would have complained at the salon, but alas I just put on a smile, payed them and left, vowing to never go back. Bottom line: If you have curly hair and are looking for a quality Deva cut, I suggest you go elsewhere.

text: I, like so many others out there, wanted this place to be great. I, UNlike so many others out there, think it is not. It pain's me to have to do this but I cannot give them a pass because they serve beer and are conveniently located south of Nashville/Cumberland River. I have been anticipating this opening for months. Maybe I am unfairly judging due this build up but some things cannot be overlooked. The first visit was opening day. I got an order of Wings "HOT"(2sides) and an order of white "DAMN HOT" (bone-in in breast and wing - separate). I won't quibble over tradition but it should be all one piece. It took 20 minutes, which is understandable. While waiting I spoke to the owner - Mr Bishop. A friendly man, who mentioned that the chicken they used was "all natural". I cannot believe this, as the wings and the breast were huge. All natural birds do not get big like commodity birds because they are not pumped with antibiotics and hormones, the chicken i received had to be "pumped". I would also venture to guess that the chicken was pumped or brined at the packer. This causes the raw finished product to add water weight, which makes for a juicy finished product, which this was. It also cheapens the price to the end user/owner since they are buying water (up to 15% of total weight) with their chicken. When i got home I eagerly tore into the "Damn Hot" first. It was under cooked, as blood could be seen where the drum used to be. This is uncalled for. They do not get an opening day pass because they cook 100's of pounds of chicken a week at their Meat and 3 - so they know how to cook chicken. The wings were also under cooked as it was quite the challenge to pull them apart. When poultry is properly cooked the joints should pull apart easily. These wings were to the the point that when pulled apart the breading fell off due to the degree of force needed to pry the joints apart. The meat was not firm, somewhat flabby or fleshy which, on par, brought on a gag reflex. As I write this I am constantly reminded of Chef Thomas Keller and his take on properly fried chicken, and how at Hatties this concept is totally ignored. Breading is crisp, which is accomplished by double dipping into the flour mix (think KFC extra crispy vs original recipe). All other Hot Chicken places in town single dip, which is the traditional way. I am not knocking Hatties for this, but double dipping has it drawbacks, especially when cooking the giant chickens. The chicken will brown or burn on the outside and appear done before it is cooked inside. This means the cook will have to lower the frying temp, which means greasy chicken... this may explain why the bread is not soaked, but their is puddle of grease in the bottom of the paper covered basket? Needs work here..... The bread also is smashed beyond recognition due the shear weight of the finished product.. They must be putting the chicken straight from the fryer onto the bread then applying the spice on top, as this would explain why the bread is- save a few streaks of red - white - if not soaked with fryer grease. I am tempted to get some chicken straight out the fryer to see if my thoughts are well substantiated. My guess is that will be dark brown- not burnt - but not golden brown as properly fried chicken should be. The spice mix is the strongest aspect this place has going for it. The "Hot" is the best I have tasted. It was hot but one could actually taste the chicken as well, everything complemented everything else - save the raw flesh. Great Job! The "Damn Hot" was hotter but not as hot as Princes or Pepperfire's "hot"... again in my opinion. I liked it, but it seems to be more oil or fat than spice. Princes and Pepperfire have more of paste finish compared to Hatties. The second trip to Hatties took place last Saturday night after a show. It was around midnight and there were a few customers there. Got hot tenders and damn hot wings. We ate there. The wings were huge and somewhat raw - again?!?!?! Showed the other Mr. Bishop (brothers). He offered a free dessert? Serve raw poultry and you offer free dessert? Though totally offended by this gesture, I declined and took the chicken home and finished it in the oven. Also there was no degree of difference between the hot and damn hot this time - seems as though they were both - just hot. The tenders were huge and well cooked. I liked them and the spice profile was consistent with my first visit. The sides were OK. Nothing to write home about... I will go back in a month or two, but will stick to boneless offerings and until then continue on to the east side for safer hot chicken.

After the wine arrived we knew it was time to make appetizer decisions, so we ended up getting the sampler which is hands down the best way to go. The sampler comes with one of each item, so if you're with someone else make sure you each get your own. If someone tried to take a bite of that lobster turnover with me I'd probably stab them with my fork! Make sure you save room for an entree... I ended up getting the "local pork offering" which last night was a slow roasted shoulder, served over a blend of tomatoes, eggplant, and spices. text: I went to Ariano's on a Saturday night around 6 pm. We were promptly greeted and seated by the friendly host. We sat upstairs on the 3rd floor which gave us an incredible view of the paintings on the ceiling; such a pretty sight! The food in this restaurant is devine! We were with a party of 5 and ate lots of heavenly food! I'll start with the appetizers...our group ordered mussels in red sauce. These yummy suckers were served in a delicious bread bowl. The mussels were served hot and they were so tasty. The bread bowl was so good, we started picking at it and wound up eating that, too! We also ordered two salads. The first one was called the Romangulo. It came with pistachio nuts, sliced granny smith apples, gorgonzola cheese spread throughout the salad with a red raspberry dressing, and red onions sliced nice and thin! The other salad was made with a gorgonzola cheese dressing. They were both fresh, crisp, and the portion was plentiful. We shared with our group since the portions were so big! Another person in our party ordered the Zia Ernesta which is mozzarella with fresh tomatoes and olives...the word fresh does not do the tomato quality justice. These tomatoes were so yummy it was like they were just picked from the vine. Oh, dear, don't let me forget the meatballs! These were on special the evening we went and we were told they may go on the late night menu as a permanent food choice. We told our waiter they should be put on the regular menu --- yes, they are that good! These meatballs were seriously the size of softballs. We had ordered two plates of these. They have cheese on the inside of the meatballs, and there is also melted cheese draped on the top of them. The red sauce on top of the meatballs complemented this appetizer. One person at my table made a comment about how he could eat 10 of thee things. He's right! They were incredible! I'm a big carb person, so found the fresh bread they served us to be heaven! The bread was hearty, and fresh from the oven! A carb queen's dream come true! Pass the butter, please! We wound up sharing all of the entrees since there were so many of us. Two people in my party had the filet...out of this world and cooked to perfection! The filets were covered in a glaze with gorgonzola cheese on top. Another person had a seafood medley type of dish which was called Otino Cioppino. This dish had snapper, shrimp, bay scallops, calamari, mussels, clams, and hot sausage served over risotto. The dish was HUGE and delicious, to say the least. It was served with a red sauce that was to die for! Another person had the Pazzo Marco which is Panko Crusted Lobster Risotto balls stuffed with lump crab meat...and lots of it! It was covered in a basil pesto sauce with and fontina cheese. This dish was in my top 2 favorite of the evening. It was amazingly delicious! I ordered the Esperanza entree. This was my other favorite entree of the evening. It's spinach and ricotta cheese layered between lightly breaded eggplant served with a vodka. Again, a huge hit at my table! The bread crumb layers were just the right amount and the eggplant was super delish! The sauce served on top of this entree was a homerun hit! Many of the entrees we ordered came with a baked potato and vegetables. The veggies looked like they were grilled. They were fresh and cooked just right! Now....onto the improtant part...dessert! Our group shared a thin crusted pizza dessert that was covered in nutella. If you're a fan of this hazelnut chocolate spread, this is the dish for you! Each slice had a fresh strawberry on it and a sprinkling of powdered sugar. We ordered a bunch of gelato and athey brought us a bunch of sppons so we could share it. My favorite of the evening was the cinnamon, which tasted like a yummy for your tummy cinnamon cookie! We also tried lemon...the taste was very refreshing! There was also a hazelnut gelato which was decadent, and a vanilla that had chocolate swirled through it. Is there any better way to end your evneing of good food? Yes! With the dessert they served us! It was unreal! Our waiter was funny, kind and most importantly attentive. He met our ever need throughout our dining experience at this restaurant. He made sure we were happy and had everything we needed throughout the evening. What more could a girl want? The owner of the restaurant came around to each table to chat and find out how everyone's meals were. What good customer service! He was friendly, attentive, and made sure our dining experience was the best on possible! We let him know how happy we were with our food and overall dining experience. Really, it doesn't get any better than this restaurant! I highly recommend this Ariano's --- it was a huge hit for everyone at our table. We will definitley be returning back for one of the best dining experiences we ever had ! Cheers to Ariano's!

text: Hands down, this is the best dentist I've ever visited. I've never enjoyed seeing the dentist, ever. I've actually avoided going ever since I made it out into the world on my own. The Initial Call: Aubrey, the receptionist, was very polite and did not give me any attitude whatsoever when I asked for some estimates as well as availability. A few other offices had given me an exasperated "We can't tell you until we see you". I was sincerely appreciative of this. Aubrey even informed me that the dentists could both evaluate my condition and likely extract the tooth on the same day. The Check-In: Quick and seamless. I told them my name, they gave me some forms to fill out and that, as they say, was that. After maybe ~5 minutes I was brought back. The X-Ray and Consultation: Again, wonderful. Han, I believe her name was, was very friendly and talked me through the process. She had a very gentle touch when putting the piece you need to bite down on for the X-Ray. Dr. Jordan Pilling soon came in and explained to me what I was looking at, with respect to the extraction. He insisted on a secondary, admittedly more pricey, X-Ray because he found the first one was not quite showing the end root of the tooth in question. After the second X-Ray was done, he explained more risks associated with the procedure and explained the nerve in my jaw that could potentially be affected by the extraction. In a display of true integrity and character, the good Dr. said I would not be charged for the second X-Ray as it was "Just for him" and did not give any more insight than the previous X-Ray. After signing a few waivers, I was told to lay back as the anesthetics were administered. The Extraction: There was a lot of pressure, maybe about 10 minutes or so of just "feeling" a push in my mouth. Dr. Pilling applied enough anesthetic that I felt 0 pain and out came the bloodied stump that had been making me miserable. I was given a small packet explaining proper care, as well as time to ask any questions I needed. They asked me what my preferred pharmacy was and then I was off to settle my tab, the scariest part of any dental visit. The Tab: $270 for the total affair. Dr. Pilling did not charge for the secondary X-Ray, which he ultimately deemed ineffective and after a quick signing of my debit slip I was off to get my pain meds and begin the healing process. text: I attended Sierra Tucson in September of 2009. I have to admit that as a person who is alcoholic the last thing I wanted to do was receive treatment for an addiction I didn't think I had. Upon getting to Sierra Tucson, not only was I in denial about my alcohol addiction, but I was resentful, apathetic and frankly didn't want anything to do with recovery, counselors or sobriety. What I found at Sierra Tucson was the real me. The 30 days I spent in rehab was more about discovery than anything else. It was the beginning of my recovery which I still practice today. It wasn't easy and I don't think it was supposed to be. My team counselor had me examine my behaviors and patterns of thinking which led me there. What I discovered changed my life forever. The team at Sierra Tucson helped me start a process which replaced shame and guilt, as the result of trauma and alcoholism, with understanding and compassion. My wife and brother attended family week. This week helped my family and I understand how my addiction affected everyone around me, especially the ones who loved me most. This precious week also started a process of repairing the relationships I damaged as the result of my drinking. Sierra Tucson also counseled my family and led them in the direction of recovery as well. Their experiential therapy was very diverse and was beneficial for me. The nurses were not only there to dispense medication, but were there to lend an ear when I was down and in a bad place. When I left Sierra Tucson I was able to understand a little more clearly what drove me to this destructive behavior. I live life today free of alcohol and am still in recovery. If anyone is thinking of attending Sierra Tucson I would advise that all it takes to make the most of their stay is open mindedness, willingness and honesty. There is hope out there and the staff of Sierra Tucson truly understands. If you are suffering from addiction then I would recommend Sierra Tucson as the starting point to your recovery. text: Horrible. Never Again. Owner is ridiculous. I have tried Palazzio's and Pascucci's a few times in the past. I preferred the former but some of my friends liked the latter. Either way, the food at both of those establishments are not great, but not god awful either. Mediocre is a good adjective for them both. The difference however is in the service and that is why I am writing this. My girlfriend and I along with my brother and his date wanted some late night tiramisu for desert (it was roughly 9:30 give or take). And we figured we would stop by Pasucci for the free bread and dessert. We were seated promptly and we decided to also order the lasagna while we waited since my girlfriend had never tried the place. Well the lasagna came out at the same time with the tiramisu. And the edges of it tasted just fine however as I started eating toward the center it was cold. I called the server over and told her about it and she said they could warm it back up for me. Not get me a new one ... but warm that one back up. I was a bit confused but whatever no biggie. I thought about it briefly while she was there and then I asked her if I could just have it taken off the bill since it came cold and did not want to wait for it (I ate less than 3 bites of it so far). She said that she would have to ask the owner. When she came back she told us that we could either pay full price and they would RE-WARM it back up for us, or they could charge us half price and we could take it home and warm it there. That is when I stared at her in disbelief and proclaimed I have never had this happen before. NEVER have I received that as a response from a restaurant that was in the wrong. Especially for being a Santa Barbara local and eaten there and tipped healthily many times before. I was pretty upset and told her to ask her owner again. The owner came back personally and gave us the check saying that she took the lasagna off the bill (like she was doing us this HUUUGE favor) and that she would instead charge us for the two bread baskets. Yes the bread baskets that are ALWAYS FREE. Apparently having two bread baskets gets you charged if all you ordered is a tiramisu, two drinks, and a cold lasagna. The best part was that when we left, the server told us that the lasagna was probably cold because the kitchen was cleaning up when we came in and took it out a bit early. Well that makes it all better does it not?
label: NEG

text: Is there another Patisserie in Indy? Yes, yes, we have other bakeries... but do we have another patisserie? Having crafted baked goods... err... baked greats under the same roof as great coffee (in City Market) shifts my routine of when & where I take in bulk calories. I hate cake. But I love coffee cake. What gives? Coffee cake can be a bit wee bit more savory. They have brioche with shaved almonds. I would gladly accept this as a gift if you feel any pity for me or need to score points with me. If I worked across the street, I'd be down here every other hour and I'd really get to know the cops that kick it around this stand. Don't think because it's a vendor stand in City Market that it doesn't have a full flight of treats because it does. And let's note something: dessert gets a bad wrap for being over-indulgent. Just plan ahead. And maybe this will get you back into exercising. Have your cake, eat it, and jog it off, too.

text: Born and raised in Philadelphia spoiled my ass as to what was/is good pizza. Pizza in the Montgo burbs suck in general, however I may have found a good one among the pathetic bunch. I was at a party a few weeks back, they had 4 pizzas from Maple Glen Pizza, a reliable local spot so I was told. And, if the rumors I heard are true, these are the former owners of Nino's Pizza on Rt 611. Not that I know that rumor to be true, but coincidental Sicilian evidence may give it credence. One of the pizzas was a Sicilian, you know, that thick crispy and nicely greasy crust pizza which in public most women say they don't like it because of "all the dough", but in secret wolf down piece after piece when no one is looking. This pizza was and is utterly amazing. The taste is as I remember from years ago, yes, that good to remember. The other pizzas include a regular, pepperoni, and a boardwalk pizza (the flip side of a regular). The sauce was terrific, the cheese of good mafia quality, and the crust thin and almost crisp. As far as the boardwalk pizza, I am not a fan, neither at the boardwalk nor here. Overall, a notch below South Philly and Rome, and ten notches above anything else around here.

text: Late last year, disaster struck. My Ipod died and the CD player in the old truck was acting funny. I was forced to rely on radio for a couple of weeks. Naturally, I set it to 91.3. Let me preface this by saying I have diverse taste in music. There is no genre which I can't enjoy, if it's performed skillfully. That said, in those two weeks the vast majority of the tracks played were pure rubbish. In the past, I remember enjoying some of Al Perry's show, and the zydeco show would play some decent cuts. The late night blues show is the only reason I'm giving the station two stars instead of one. The DJ will often have themed shows, and attempt to educate the listeners about the history of the music. The "Res Radio" show paints a portrait of Tucson's native residents as nothing more than uneducated gang members. I could take all the medicine in my cabinet and still be offended by the musical content of the "Medicine Cabinet" show. Imagine a three year old banging on a saucepan and a Casio keyboard. This stuff's so underground it should be buried. We live in a world filled with great music. Maybe KXCI could try playing a little of it?

text: BBP didn't quite knock my socks off, there are more than a few missteps with the place. Burgers are good and I like the flavor combinations they offer. Definitely more creative than other casual burger joints, e.g. goat cheese/lemon honey mustard/ arugula, or avocado/watercress/cheddar. They also offer a couple of unique table-side sauces for your burger: jalapeño sauce (tasty), burger sauce ( a little 'raisiny" but good) chipotle ketchup. Prices are ok (wish they had some kind of combo meal...burger, fries, drink), but kid prices are very reasonable. Staff is affable and attentive. Here are some problems that will prevent BBP from getting an unqualified recommendation in my book: - Burgers are suspiciously juicy. When you bite into the burger there appears to be a "pocket" that was created to hold scalding hot liquid. I find it hard to believe that this liquid is naturally occurring, I've never come across an experience like this (and I've had, and cooked, plenty of juicy burgers in my day) where after biting into a burger, liquid comes pouring all over you and the plate. - Why do they ask me how I want my burger cooked? I ask for med-rare, but they ALWAYS give it to me well-done (and again, their well done still has an abundance of the "juice") -Fries can often be a problem .....many times the fries are small fragments and burnt. Don't bother splurging on fries if you're on a diet...they aren't worth it. - Also, fries come with Bobby's Fry Sauce.....so watery...so bland. It's orange in color, watery in texture and has no taste. No sure what the deal is there. I know that it seems that I just knocked BBP around a bit, but there's no reason for a place owned by an Iron Chef to have so many crappy aspects about it. Yes the burgers and good, the toppings creative, but overall they are missing the mark.
label: NEG

text: I discovered this clinic 4 years ago when my guinea pig became fatally ill, and they were the only clinic I could find at the time who would treat exotic animals on an emergency basis. They sent me a sympathy card signed by all staff, which was very touching. Since then, all of my parents' pets, my dog and cat, and several friends' pets have become regulars at Calgary Trail Pet Hospital. It is really obvious that all the staff are passionate about the welfare of animals, and I always feel comfortable and confident in their knowledge of my cat's and dog's healthcare needs. Every time I go in, I feel like they not only value my business, but that it's important that even the smallest creatures get the best care possible. I've bounced around to many different vet clinics in the past, and Calgary Trail Pet Hospital is by far the best one in the city. I highly recommend this clinic to anyone and everyone!

Check out their website, under the Exhibits tab, to learn more about each inhabitant and how it came to the World Bird Sanctuary. It was really cool to see these magnificent birds up close. We saw several different kinds of owls, eagles and hawks. There were also chickens, cranes, turkeys, parrots, pelicans...even a raven named Lenore. It's a pretty cool resource located in Valley Park. text: I'm not from New Orleans but for some reason Hurricane Katrina hit me really hard. After that, my husband and I made a pact that we would visit NOLA every year to help bolster their economy. Guess what? We've made true on that promise, even visiting twice in one year. When I saw that they were going to do a Katrina exhibit I was looking forward to it but at the same time, I was a little reluctant as well. Like most of the exhibits I've seen at this museum, this one is exceptionally well done. It's touching, it's poignant, and yes, it's also very sad. I teared up on more than one occasion... The facility itself is great - right in the heart of the French Quarter. The people who work here (or are they volunteers?) are amazing. They do need to build a few more bathrooms... All that being said, I hope they make this exhibit a semi-permanent display. Not so that we can dwell on the past... rather, so that people can see just how strong the citizens of New Orleans are and how far they've come since then. I'm sure there will be people out there who will nay-say what I've written but my admiration for NOLA comes from a genuine place. Great exhibit and a wonderful city.

text: Searching for a restaurant that has offerings for vegans and people with dairy issues can be tough. Not only does Gourmet Pizza company accommodate both, but they also have a lot of gluten free offerings - something very rare for a pizza joint. And I guess if you're vegan or have gluten allergies, just about any pizza that you're actually able to eat without dying (physically or just emotionally) is probably a great treat. Our vegan friends had tried their pizza at a vegetarian festival, liked it and suggested we go there since we were nearby. The problem is that if you're not limited to vegan/GF options, the pizza really isn't that great. It's not bad, but it's pretty mediocre. If you're adventurous, you can try crawfish tails or escargot on your pizza. Interesting, but I just wasn't in the mood for snails on my pizza - just some pepperoni, thanks. Had it just been a matter of the pizzas, I would have gone 2.5 stars, rounded to 3. But we also got an order of the pizza breadsticks and my wife ordered the Mayan salad. The breadsticks are covered in melted mozzarella and then an entire block of parmesan is grated and dumped on top. The result is a very dry taste that is somewhat ameliorated by the tomato dipping sauce. Unfortunately, the cup of it is so small that you only get about 2-3 breadsticks dipped in there before you're out. The biggest complaint, though, was the Mayan salad. To call this salad "crappy" would be a compliment. Made up entirely of romaine hearts and a handful of tasteless beans, corn, tomatoes and cheese - not even the mango dressing could help it. The only thing gourmet about this place is the toppings list.
label: NEG

text: I have never in my life had a few beers and then got a craving for bone-marrow. Put some nachos on the menu or something...trust me, no one will complain. I really want to like this place. I live about a block and a half away and the area is in serious need of a good bar/restaurant. First off, the place has a minimalistic decor but its nice. Restored wood lines the ceiling and most of the walls. The bar is simple with a chalkboard drink list. It is small but seems to have a decent amount of seating. The kitchen is in the back but open so you can check out their handywork. The open layout allows you to see the two tv's from anywhere in the restaurant although I think the layout also makes the place a little loud. As for the beer list, it is OK. They had about 10-12 beers on tap, a few beers were interesting and the rest were local staples, no macros except for the obligatory $3 pbr pounders and high lifes. Seems to be a lot of love going to Philly Brewing Company as they had the most beers on the draft list. The nonhappy hour prices are OK, in the $4-$6 range for a beer. I'd be way more jazzed about the place if they did half off happy hours but as far as I know they only do $1 off all beers. As for the cocktails, I didn't try any but they have a list of some of their own specialties. Once again, I'd be more interested in these drinks if they would settle down in price to more of the $8 range rather than the $10-$12 range. The group sitting next to me ordered a punch bowl called Mummer's Punch. It's 4quarts of punch to share and looked fun. It is supposed to serve 4-6 people and costs $45. Menu wise I'm not sure what is going on here. I think the chef designing the menu was over-ambitious, unaware of what the clientele in the area is looking for, and would prefer to be cooking at a gourmet restaurant rather than at a South Philly bar. Basically, the only thing on the menu that you would recognize as pub food is the burger and wings. The other options include things like bone marrow, pulled duck bbq, and tartare. Don't get me wrong, I like all sorts of food, and I would be interested in trying some of the things on the menu but the menu should be more balanced. For example, if you want to offer bone marrow then fine, but offer pulled pork bbq instead of pulled duck...sometimes I don't want to order food and hope that its good. I want to order something that I know I like and then hope that the restaurant makes it really well so I end up loving it. Price wise, the menu is a little too expensive as well. They have 'small plates' and large plates' I'm not sure how big the small plates are but they are in the $10 range and the large places move up to the $18-$22 range. So basically, if my wife and I go here, have a beer or cocktail each, then each have an entree we are looking at spending $60 plus dollars. That's a lot of money for a bar in Pennsport. I'll go to The Village Belle for a dinner in that price range any day. At least you are getting some non-bar ambiance there. I did see someone with the steak frites which looked really good but at $18 most of the entrees are too expensive to make this a place to go and get a beer and dinner when I don't want to cook. The service was good even though the place was crowded. And when you consider that I was there when they had only been open for 2 or 3 days, it was running very smoothly. As far as the places association or their claim to cater to people working the the restaurant/bar "Industry" I didn't see it. I don't know if they offer a discount to industry folks, but it didn't appear to be advertised on the menu or anything. The only thing that seemed to give a nod to the industry were little bits of advice given on menu's and coasters and things such as "Tip: Never start your order with, "this is going to be a pain but...". There is also an offer on the drink menu to buy a round of shots or a six pack for the kitchen. I guess this caters to "the industry" but mostly just to people who work at "the industry" and not the restaurant biz in general. Overall, I don't really care about "the industry" theme. I'm not in the business so it doesn't have any impact on me, I just thought they might have a little more playing off the theme. It mostly feels gimmicky With all of this said, I want to note that this is my initial review. The place is young and I live so close I'm sure I'll be back. I want the place to find an identity that is more appropriate for the neighborhood and clientele. I'm not saying serve coors light and fill the place with Mummers. I just mean, recognize that The Industry is not in Center City or Rittenhouse. If you are catering to people in the "Industry" realize that you have to understand that you are a bar and have to offer a good happy hour or nightly specials along with understandable food at a reasonable price not gourmet-based food. I'll be back, but I'm hoping for change.

text: I went to college in Oxford, MS where the original McAlister's started and was excited to see a branch opening near me in New Orleans. I've always been a fan of their McAlister's Club sandwich, but I like to dip it in extra honey mustard. Initially, getting extra honey mustard for dipping wasn't that much of a challenge, but recently the service and accuracy in fulfilling orders has gone downhill rapidly. If I place a phone order for pick-up, I'm lucky to get the extra honey mustard without asking for it again at pick-up (even though it's noted on my receipt). I placed an order via their website recently and not only did I not get the extra honey mustard on the side, I didn't get any on the sandwich either. Today I ordered my usual, and the guy taking my order repeated everything back to me, including the "extra honey mustard on the side"...but instead of getting what I ordered my sandwich came out absolutely dripping in mustard. I wouldn't mind so much except that I almost never eat the entire sandwich at one time and by the time I'm ready to eat the rest the extra mustard has turned the bread into mush. I have contacted McAlister's on multiple occasions about their poor service but it hasn't seemed to make any difference. Maybe they'll make some changes if their public reviews are bad enough.

text: Second visit to Pescatore was disappointing. Service tonight was very spotty. Seems like the restaurant is understaffed. Table was not ready when we arrived and we had to wait 10 minutes in the alcove. Another long wait before waitress came for our order. When we were done with our appetizers, she came by to clear the plates and, seeming frazzled, said "were those your appetizers or your entrees?" As far as food, the appetizers of eggplant rollatini and mushroom stuffed with crabmeat were both excellent. We didn't fare that well with the entrees, however. My stuffed pork chop was underdone (had to send it back to the kitchen) and the linquine pescatore was underwhelming. Other than garlic and oil, it seems to have no sauce. text: This was a big disappointment. Twice. I usually like to give a place the benefit of the doubt if they aren't great the first time around. In this case, The Toni Roni Special pizza. The second is that if a restaurant wins anything for a menu item (even the popularity contest that is the Best of Philly), it's worth a try. Working from the bottom up, since it's the dough that makes a pizza, you have a soft and floppy center. If you've ever taken an Elio's pizza out of the toaster oven about halfway through cooking, it's like that. Sure, it's edible if you're really hungry but it doesn't support the weight of the sauce, cheese and toppings and just folds over, dumping said cheese and toppings on your plate. The outer crust was ok. If the whole pizza had that crispness, it might have been a serviceable pie. The sauce is ok, I can't complain about anything there. The toppings though were bland and generally under done. The sausage looked it was steamed or boiled. There's no excuse for that when you have a grill. Like I said, I do like to give a place a 2nd chance so naturally I went with one of their tomato pies since it was voted Best of Philly. Sometimes less is more, this was one of those times. I ordered the Sinatra which is one of their tomato pie with mozzarella and basil on the top. Sounds great, right? Starting from the bottom up again, the crust was very crisp, almost hard and brittle. Ok, it's not what I'm used to but it was ok. Although it was sort of like eating a bowl of captain crunch, the roof of your mouth gets scraped up a bit. Still, it was tasty, I just wish it had a little more body to it. The sauce was pretty good, it had some texture to it, some real tomato and not just a paste, which was nice. The mozzarella though was bland and rubbery and the slices were about the size of quarters, maybe a half dollar. The idea was good but it's a total waste to put low quality cheese on a decent pizza. So that's that, I won't be going back again, ever.

text: I'm giving Zama 2-stars purely because my reasonable expectation was no where near met. Staff just to be fair were friendly and very nice. This is really a review of the food. Miso Soup: Basic and very average in quality. Avocado, yellowtail, jalapenos and tuna sashimi all came together nicely. I'm a fool for sushi with a kick. If you are going to go here, order that roll. Sushi & Sashimi Combo: Major let-down. The sashimi tasted awefully like it had been refrozen if not once a few times, and not very well, you know, that day old lacking freshness taste. If you don't know what I mean, go eat what I find to be great sashimi at Fat Salmon or Vic Sushi and compare it to Zama. The Sushi wasn't put together all to well, almost as if they give the intern/new guy the simple sushi. Portions were not very large, and lacked satisfactory flavor. Drinks: I had a lychee fizz which wasn't too bad really. My other half however had the candy cane martini (drink of the season). It made me want to gag but she managed to power through its bitter over mintiness. And for all this... we paid the supreme price of $100. This is the only time I've felt foolish paying a large sum for sushi. I'd have valued it all at $60 MAX and with the quality it wasn't even really worth that. The location is literally just around the corner from where I used to stay and it would have been nice to get a good well valued sushi experience here. text: My girlfriend was raving about Philly Indonesian food so we finally got the chance to make the drive down the turnpike from Jersey...WOW, unbelievably glad we did! To preface this, I have eaten at numerous Indonesian places in Queens, NY, and am a big fan of Asian comfort food (doesn't matter if it is Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Malaysian, or anything else I missed!) and have seen too many mediocre bowls of "noodles". Not gonna lie, the area threw me off a bit. Im not used to having to park a larger car backing into a tiny spot in a cramped street. I felt like my mirrors were going to become the casualties of the six young kids playing ball up and down the small row. The area was a little suspect, as we already passed over another place due to its really shady look neighborhood. I will venture for good food any day, but sometimes instinct tells you to keep moving! I gotta say, walking in felt like I had grown up down the block. It just emanated that local, unpretentious, warm feeling that is lost in some of the shiny, new, plasticky restaurants I see so often in North Jersey. 10 or so tables, small staff, a refrigerator filled with desserts, and the familiar smells of the feast to come fill your senses. We ordered fried wontons, mie komplit (#1 on noodle page), the spicy salted fish entree, and the pork combination (#18 on entrees page). The wontons were surprisingly thin and flavorful. Very crunchy, definitely different than the ones you usually get at a corner Chinese spot. The mie komplit comes with egg noodles, roasted pork, and ground beef amongst some bright greens and fried onions. You are given a separate bowl with chicken broth and some fish cake/meatballs floating playfully in it. It's up to you to either douse your noodles into a full on soup or just enough so everything retains its separate and delicious flavors and textures. I say drop in a little at a time, it really brings everything together in the most wonderful way. It was warm and delicious! The salted fish was exactly as advertised, spicy as all hell! Dude, these chiles are some demon reincarnate spitting hot fire onto all of your taste buds, at the same time meshing really well with what should be an overly salted piece of fried fish. They come with some tasty sides, a deep fried or soy sauce marinated egg (both hard boiled and equally worth having), and a substantial portion of rice. I found it a bit hellfire for my taste but my girlfriend loved it. The combination pork platter was a trio of swine...sausage slices, pork belly, and roasted pork. The sweet, salty, and savory combinations were on point, and the accompanying pickles, rice, eggs, and chile-potatoes are enough to leave you full and sated to the point of food coma. I would eat this and the mie komplit as a glut-lunch with take home for dinner any day of the week. We ended up ordering a fried chicken entree, another mie komplit, and rice cake curry to go, as well as two delicious homemade cookie desserts...yeah we may have overdone it a bit. All in all, one appetizer, six entrees, and two desserts...grand total of under sixty bucks! All that damn goodness for about 7 bucks a pop! Worth it...stop reading and go already!

text: This really is a beautiful place. In addition to the Sonoran Desert Museum and Saguaro National Park, you need to visit here if you are in town. I recommend riding the shuttle to the top of the canyon and walking down until you get tired. Keep your ticket then ride the shuttle the rest of the way. The shuttle drivers give a decent tour. There is a significant change in elevation from the start to end. At the next-to-last shuttle stop from the top, walk down to the creek and climb around on one of the biggest blocks of rock you've ever seen and see how the creek has carved it up. If it is hot, plan on a hat, sunscreen, and a good sized bottle of water. This is the desert. We hiked over Christmas with a medium jacket. Get off the main road and walk some of the single-track trails. Seeing the vegetation up close is awesome. The desert is special. There is a network of dirt paths. Spend some time in the visitor's center before your excursion so you can get familarized with the plants and animals of the area, so you know what you'll be seeing. text: My wife and I went on a tapa style restaurant crawl over the weekend starting at Barbuzzo (which was as delicious as ever). Towards the end of our meal we asked our bartender about any good restaurant recs in the area, and he mentioned that The Oyster House on Sansom had just undergone some sort of renovation/change in ownership and it was GOOD. (Not sure how long ago this happened, but I vaguely remember reading a review in the Inquirer a while back). Anyway, being a beautiful June evening we wandered the few blocks down Sansom, and walked into the Oyster House. The place was hopping, and just before we sat down I noticed the specials board stated that they were running $1 Happy Hour oysters from 9-11 pm on Saturday. It was Saturday, and about 7:30pm, so being the cheap bastard that I am, we left and carried on down the street to Tinto (review soon to come), and The Dandelion Pub (battle rap style review soon to come). Upon our return, the place was jammed. Not a seat was to be had at the enormous bar that snakes it's way through the whole restaurant. The place was crowded with a mix of couples out on the town (like us), tables of friends, and a smattering of hipsters. Nobody was overly dressed, and very few people looked like they had just rolled out of bed. The two lovely hostesses promptly took my name, told us to grab a drink if we wanted, and that they would find us as soon as two seats opened up. Once at the bar, I had to inquire about the champagne special. Apparently, it comes in a can. I declined, and ordered a $3 Preininger, I mean Kenzinger, and my wife had a glass of house white. Both of us approved of our drinks. I had never had Kenzinger before, and found it a crisp refreshing pilsner perfectly suited for the weather, and some oysters. Speaking of oysters, the bartender told us that the $1 Happy Hour special only refers to the oyster of the day, which was a Delaware Bay oyster, not a choice of any of the 6 other oysters they offer. Being unsure of whether I have ever tried a Delaware Bay oyster, I was almost as apprehensive about the prospect of eating something out of the scummy Delaware Bay as I was about the champagne in a can. After quickly being seated at the bar, my wife and I both agreed that we'd be brave, and order just 6 of them in case they were repulsive. Thankfully, they were not, and we quickly ordered six more. The oysters were medium in size, had very low salinity, and were extremely creamy in the mouth. I liked them. Can't believe I just wrote the line, creamy in the mouth, but dammit they were. My only gripe was that the oysters were not fully shucked, and were still attached to the shell. Also, there was absolutely no oyster liquor in the shell. Not sure if it that is due to the kind of oyster, but I like the juice. Being the last stop on the tapa crawl, we decided to call it a night, but vowed we'd return for more. Apparently, they offer something called "Tuesday Night Dump Dinner". As unappetizing as it sounds, it looks like a Pile O' Seafood. I am good with that. And for 19 bucks, I am good with that, too. I definitely, enjoyed our brief snack, and was impressed with the fantastic service from both hostesses, and bartenders. The bartenders were swamped, but they handled it with ease, and personable service. Also, loved the seafood house decor with a myriad of oyster plates decorating the walls. We are both excited to return, and will hopefully make it back for Dump Night.

Look at the other tables and see the size of the sandwiches if you're curious-- and if you think you're still going to be hungry, order the plate of fries to SHARE, or you're not going to be able to finish at least one thing on your table. The service is generally stellar and I would recommend making reservations, because the place gets very crowded (especially at brunch!). The thing to keep in mind is that, yes, it is loud, and yes, there are tons of kids. But it's a fifties style diner, so try to deal. text: So to put it lightly, my mom (who lives in Tucson) doesn't get out much. So while visiting her I came up with the brilliant plan of taking her out for a drive up to Mt. Lemmon for an afternoon trip. I hadn't taken the drive for years and years, so we gas up the rental and head out. The drive is absolutely beautiful, especially during the non-summer months. Although the last time I was up there, it was during the summer...which means that in the course of the drive, you will go from scorching temperatures down in the Tucson valley to much cooler weather as your climb the mountain (at least a 20-30 degree drop). The drive takes you up the 9,000 plus foot mountain with plenty of breathtaking views of Tucson and once you get to the top of the mountain, views of the Oro Valley also come into view. On this particular trip, the upper elevations were covered with quite a bit of snow. Summerhaven is a community located near the summit of the mountain but much of the community is being rebuilt due to the 2003 Aspen Fire. There are many vista points where vehicles can pull over and passengers can take in the many amazing views Mt. Lemmon has to offer. It's quite amazing to watch the progression of the environment as you climb the mountain. You start with mainly cactus littered desert...leading up to rocky mountain passes...and eventually bringing you to mountainous forest covered with huge pine trees. Besides being a drive, you can also hike...picnic...ski...and off-road down the backside towards the town of Oracle. There is a park fee for visitors who plan to do more than just drive up and back down. Definitely a place for anyone in Tucson to visit if they love natural beauty and spectacular views.

text: This is one of those reviews that I'm really hoping someone at management will read and deal with. The thing is, though, that Pei Wei makes a really fantastic Pad Thai. I will continue to come back for that, but my orders will probably stay in the take-out category. I want to emphasize that some restaffing needs to be done, or more staff training or something, because I normally enjoy Pei Wei. I asked if the fish could be just grilled, without the butter, but the server recommended against it. Though the fish itself was cooked perfectly, nice and flaky, I'd swear there was a pound of salt in the rub. The shrimp and eggplant side was the highlight of the dinner -- very tasty. This was a company meal with locals that loved the place, so I didn't complain, but this wasn't close to the meals I've had in the French Quarter or, in most other cajun places in other place. text: Since it has opened, Tashan has been on my list of places to try and their recent restaurant week special sealed the deal. And so a friend and I came here for dinner. We started with a white wine blend, which was tasty and served nicely chilled. We also got the "flat" water, which tasted like it had been filtered after coming out of the tap -- nice. For food, we started with the octopus, which was expertly roasted so as to border on having a crunchy exterior and was served with a tasty sauce; it was some of the best octopus I've had, in terms of both texture and flavor. Next we had the scallops. These were nicely fire roasted, but fire roasting didn't work as well for the scallops as for the octopus; still tasty, but I prefer other preparations. The scallops were accompanies by a nice sauce, but would have been better with, say, a veggie puree. Next we had the "Indian" portions of the meal. The butter chicken was superb. The free-range chicken tasted distinctly better than typical mass-market restaurant chicken. And the sauce was so good. The accompanying rice was great for absorbing that sauce. So was the delicious garlic-onion-cilantro (g.o.c.) naan. Finally, the mixed-vegetable and rice hot pot was nice -- especially the baked-bread lid on top -- but could have used some more sauce (we made do with butter chicken sauce). We were nicely stuffed after all that and we skipped dessert. The servers were friendly and were reasonably prompt in refilling glasses of water and wine. It seemed a bit excessive, though, that we dealt with about seven different staff people. First, it's a bit disconcerting to have a new face for every other interaction and, second, if you think it'd be impressive or something to have some sort of service ballet, get it right, and make sure that each person on the team knows what the others have done (which, of course, is practically impossible in a restaurant). The decor was subtly lit dark wood and leather with some color provided by flowers; I feel kinda neutral about it. The prices were on the high side, but not eye-popping.

The tables themselves are big enough to seat a bunch of people, and you can move them together if you have a crowd -- you can easily have ten people sitting together and feel like you can have a conversation with everyone at the table. It's a perfect setup for large groups, but I've been just as comfortable going with just one other person. Anyway, are you in? Of course you are. Places like these are pure gold in a town like this. If you've never been to 1702, you really owe it to yourself to give it a shot. So why only four stars? For one thing, the service can be hit-or-miss, especially when it gets super busy. Granted, it's always difficult for staff when there are huge crowds of hungry and thirsty people, and that is no doubt exacerbated by the complexity of the menu. It also bears mentioning that some of the folks on the staff are absolutely incredible, and that the hits have certainly outweighed the misses. But some nights it has felt like our server was not even glancing in our direction to assure us that we would be attended to soon, and that can be really frustrating when folks have been waiting for a while. For another thing, the food is good but not incredible, and if you opt for a gourmet slice (which I often do), you're shelling out a little more than 8 bucks for a piece of pizza (before tax and tip). That's pretty expensive -- about the same expenditure at Zachary's will get you a slice of higher-quality pizza AND a pretty good beer. But those caveats shouldn't distract from the main point here, which is that 1702 is totally epic and totally worth visiting, especially if you like beer. Maybe I'll see you there!

text: Maxine's Chicken and Waffles is a unique restaurant as far as Indianapolis goes. While we have a number of soul food restaurants, Maxine's is the only place around that can boast specializing in chicken and waffles, a combination that anyone I know has only tried at Roscoe's out in California. In addition to these two, they serve up a plethora of burgers, catfish, greens, fried cornbread with their signature peach butter, eggs...just about any good home style country food you could want. And everything they do (that I tried, at least), they do well. I was downtown at the City-County Building with two friends to help support the Sinking Ship, which was having a hearing to get their liquor license renewed (and which they were granted.) Before the hearing, driving down East Street, we passed by Maxine's. I had heard tales of thick, delicious waffles and crispy, well-seasoned fried chicken from friends, but had never taken the opportunity to stop there myself. As the hearing was at nine in the morning and didn't get out until nearly noon, and considering none of us had eaten, the time was right for a visit. We were greeted by a large gentleman who was very friendly and showed us to our table. Our waitress was very kind as well, and though busy, was attentive to our every need, including bringing us crayons so we could draw on our place mats (yes, I'm thirty and I occasionally like to color~) Each of us got a wing and a waffle, which at $5 is a deal. Maxine's menu includes five meals for $5, and they bring the first round of fried corn muffins and peach butter out for free. I got a blueberry waffle, as did another friend, while the third got the sweet potato waffle. While all were delicious and served with another heaping helping of the peach butter, the sweet potato waffle stands out at the winner; spiced like pumpkin pie, it may be the best waffle in Indianapolis. One jumbo chicken wing and one waffle were'n't enough for me at the time, so I ordered another two jumbo wings. The standard chicken and waffle order comes with three jumbo wings, and I debated about ordering that right off. Luckily for me, it's the same price for that standard order as it is to get the single wing and waffle, then later add two more jumbo wings. Hot sauce at the table went perfectly with the wings, and I was well satisfied as we left Maxine's. If you haven't tried Maxine's Chicken and Waffles and have a craving for some good soul food, I highly suggest trekking downtown. The culinary adventure is well worth it, as, according to the menu, there's "a taste of love in every bite."

text: I moved to SE Arizona two years ago from the Pacific Northwest, and one of the things I miss most about Seattle is that there are so many Ethiopian restaurants there. After hearing them mentioned on a local radio station, I made a beeline for Cafe Desta a week later when I was back in town. Cafe Desta's injera is -wonderful-, amongst the best I've had. I plan to go back and try more dishes, but I had the mild Lamb T'ibs and one of my favorite vegetable dishes, a cabbage/potato/carrot stew seasoned with ginger and tumeric called Ye'Atakilt Alich'a: it was perfect and simply flavorful like it should be. First I was hoping to try the Kitfo, a rather unusual 'meat tartare' sort of dish unique to this region's cooking, but I was told that the person who makes the best Kitfo was not cooking today so instead I should try the T'ibs. I was a bit hesitant to try them spicy, and will next time. They were tender and perfectly cooked, but pretty much straight lamb and onions to my palate...very good lamb though! Reading the other reviews, I must add that all my dishes were fresh and hot. I also had a guava juice and was surprised to see it was definitely not a tiny little glass, again nice to be getting reasonable portions for the cost. In Seattle, many Ethiopian restaurants are much less expensive (perhaps competitively since there are a lot) than Cafe Desta but the quality here I felt was very high, the food quite authentic, and the portions are not lacking. I wouldn't mind seeing a few more vegetarian dishes such as okra or sweet potato stews on the menu, but the essentials were here. However, I plan to return in particular for more of that -great-injera and to try the other vegetarian dishes such as the Gomen, Misir Alich'a and Fosolia, ------------ Okay here's a quick update to this review, went back for the lunch special today of three entrees of my choice, plus a side order of Ayeb (a dry cottage cheese that is a good counterpoint to spicy meats). This time I had the Kaye Asa (berbere Tilapia stew), the Fosolia and the Kik (yellow split peas). My favorites so far...the Tikil-Gomen (aka Ye'Atakilt Alich'a, sorry, I know it by another name!), the Kik and the Kaye Asa, in that order. But the Fosolia was good, just the other three are better! Oh, well of course the delicious Injera, which I needed to order an additional piece of! Another great meal, pleasant service and fresh food. text: I love this place. And frankly, I get a little agitated at some of the (small handful of) folks who feel the need to wax eloquent about the legitimacy of their southern heritage and their knowledge of southern food, and how "this is not it." All of us who were reared in the South have our own view of what good southern food is all about. We agree on some things, sure, but there's plenty of room for variety. Great southern food from low country Mississippi is quite different than great southern food from northeast Georgia. At least from this southerner's perspective, Sylvan Park serves up real southern food that is consistently good. My personal favorites are the roast beef, fried corn, cornbread, and banana pudding. (My wife is a banana pudding addict, and this is her hands-down favorite in Middle TN.) I can see how some folks, probably from different parts of the South, might not find all of Sylvan Park's food to be familiar or what they remembered from their childhood. But it does remind me of lots of the food my Granny and Granddaddy would dish up, and they were as authentically southern as it gets. Is this the "best" meat and three in Nashville? Probably not. Personally, I have never had lunch that tasted better than the freakish wonders emanating from Arnold's Country Kitchen. That being said, I've paid Sylvan Park many more visits. It feels like home, it's stress free, it's very reasonably priced, and the area is great. Give it a shot. And if it's not your cup of tea, try to appreciate that it's a legendary local hole in the wall, and that it has earned its reputation as a go-to joint for plenty of locals.

It was clear throughout the conversation that the chefs at Bella Nashville are very proud of their work. They talked extensively about the recent good reviews they had had, their booming business, and the amount of time they had been open (104 days, to be exact). All signs pointed to this being a great pizza place. I saw my pizza come out of the oven, and then watched as the girl who initially took my order meticulously placed Benton's ham and basil on my pizza; so meticulously, in fact, that my pizza was cold by the time I got it. I carried my pizza over to the table and noticed that the smell was off putting. I took one bite and knew that the almost raw ham had to be removed. After removing the ham, I took another bite. I looked at my husband and apologized for wasting $10. I asked him to take a bite, and he was reluctant based on the smell, but agreed to assure me that I wasn't crazy (I mean, how could pizza be inedible?). He agreed that the pizza was disgusting and offered to take it back to the counter. When my husband took the pizza back to the counter, the staff didn't apologize, or offer anything else. I won't go back again, and do not recommend this restaurant. Next time I want great pizza, I will head over to Coco's Italian Kitchen.

AND the thing was still hot, but not soggy or gross. As for the taste, the steak was great. Not heavenly but still pretty good. It had a good amount of both cheese and onions without either overpowering the steak. The bread was soft (and as I mentioned before, not soggy, a crucial element to quality take-out cheesesteaks) and the meat was tasty and not greasy. Considering it was $6.75 (plus $0.65 for some added hot peppers), it was reasonably priced for a nicely sized steak. Would definitely consider going back for the steaks.
