text: My experience at Bottom of the Cup was excellent! I had heard from locals (I'm new to town) that Otis was the one to be read by so the morning after a break up I made an appointment. First off- I'm not sure if he's this way with everyone, or just with me, or what, but we laughed and cracked jokes through the whole reading. I felt like he really picked up on my vibe and was able to speak to me in "my language" (which isn't so serious). I love that in a reader. He started with my palms and was incredibly accurate with my personality traits, worth ethic, etc. He reads cards in a way I'm unfamiliar with- not that there's anything wrong with that- and that was interesting. He would pick out cards that called to him and would elaborate on them. Through the reading he told me many things that directly related to how I've been feeling, changing, and gave me a lot of confirmation I'm doing the right thing in life. He of course gave me some very (VERY) detailed information about the future which time will only tell, but given his accuracy with the rest of the reading I have to say I kinda believe him! He had a few things he said to me that I'll remember for the rest of my life- he has an amazing take on life and the world and the way we work in it and I left riding home on my bike with the biggest smile on my face. Thank you Otis! My 30 minute reading was $60 and came with a CD. I highly suggest, if for nothing else, to meet a true local New Orleans character (Otis has lived in the heart of the French Quarter since the 70's I believe). A 10 minute reading will be the best $30 you'll spend- but you should opt for the 30 minute one. Enjoy!

text: I am unabashed about asking for information. If I want something, I will put on a smile and go looking. In a restaurant, I will ask about where they source x, y, or z ingredient. I will ask about preparation. I will ask what something means. I will ask about wine, beer, or cocktails. I will leave no stone unturned. Ancora was ready for me, in that respect. We asked our server to define roughly half the menu; and he did so with panache. I asked about the nuances of some of the different cheese; he had a simple explanation ready for me. I wanted wine, but I didn't recognize any of the varietals on the menu so I asked the bartender (who wasn't slammed so I didn't feel a bit guilty). I asked and asked and asked, until I was happy with the answer. And Ancora's staff kept answering me. That pleases me. So why the emphasis on questions? Because Ancora has a learning curve. With a menu that relies heavily on Italian, it can get confusing. But see, Italian is a language with a number of very specialized food words so each nuance of cheese or meat has a name. This leaves us with a delicious precision in food preparation. I am happy with the precision because it means the flavors are carefully cultivated. We had two pizzas (the daily special and the Bianca), both delicious. Between three people, two pies and an app were enough to satisfy. Now, the trick with the pizzas we ordered was compromise. One member of our party doesn't like olives or capers, both fixtures on the Bianca pizza. She agreed to try it because she was out-voted...then she loved the pizza. I think that reflects strongly on the quality of the ingredients going into each pie. Another of our number doesn't love arugula on pizza, but she didn't mind picking it off if it was too much. There wasn't a leaf left on her plate, either. I was super impressed. There is no doubt that I would return to Ancora. I'd love to see the decor change a little bit and move away from using grey as the neutral. (Art historian moment: I feel like they need a warm neutral like taupe or soft yellow to really capture the creamy, soft, crisp vibe. Grey was too cold, too industrial, too "Chipotle-esque" for my eye.) And a note on the service: They seem to have ironed out the issues other, earlier reviews noted. I can see where the service would get thin, but everyone was where they should be doing what they should be doing tonight. It was like watching a beautiful bicycle being put through its paces. I really enjoyed the cohesive nature of the service, with management blending into table service blending into the bar blending into the kitchen blending into the pizza makers. It really worked. I want to give Ancora a 5 star review, but I also want to leave room for the place to grow. My fervent hope is that I will bump this place up to a 5 star joint with my next visit. Accessibility notes: Door opens out. Fully accessible for mobility devices. Can get loud. No braille menu or signage.

Dante, also using fresh local produce, follows this great tradition but is not just doing that, they also infuse their own alcohol and barrel-age New Orleans classic cocktails. I was smitten by their new creation, Corpse Reviver, oh dizzying delight for the cocktail enthusiast. On culinary trips like this one from Chicago to New Orleans, I give up on my regular vegetarian life style, and venture out with a stop at red meat and not biting into cute little baby pigs, as already the name, sucklings, seems to forbid that. Everybody has their limits and some might argue that shrimps have cute eyes... Those we had though: the Grilled Shrimp on Stone Ground Grits with andouille red eye gravy was a down to earth amaze. The Redfish on the Half Shell topped wtih crab meat and soft herbs, the Caramelized Onion Smashed Potatoes and their famous Chicken Roasted Under a Brick, maple glazed, with a potato and bacon hash cake, topped with a fried farm egg were a taste bud's joy, and the dessert, ah, I should have left more room, Blueberry Brown Butter Upside Down Cake with creole cream cheese gelato is just heaven. Thanks to chef Eman Loubier, the mixologists and the savvy staff we got the intro to southern cooking, which makes us ask for more.

text: Short Version: Felt like I was working too hard for a mediocre, late lunch, despite the food being beautifully presented on its own. Uninterested in eating here again. Long Version: As a vegan, I was really excited to try out the new vegetarian restaurant, Esti's Besty's. I've had my fair share of hummus and pita, so I could tell you if it's a hit or a miss. If you've ever been to Maoz, I can tell you now that you can get a similar meal (with more options considering their salad bar) for less than the price offered here, with a no-bullshit customer service experience. I ordered for delivery, and being that I live 5 minutes away driving distance, I ordered around 1:30pm or so expecting an hour delivery. The driver was out at a store (or some other noise that translated into: your food will be late) but I obliged because my mind was set on local falafel & hummus. After purchasing the falafel platter and the hummus dish, what seems to be the owner said she would call me back upon his arrival. I waited about an hour for this call. Edging toward closing time without a phone call, I called and got a hurried, "He's on his way!" response, with my price check of $18.05. This unexpected range was discouraging (especially now, knowing its quality and quantity did not meet my expectations). On the Perlin's menu on allmenu's.com, their prices were marked lower. So, hearing that number after not receiving a call was disappointing, but alas, the driver was on his way, so I figured all would be well with my mind and my tummy, soon enough. Right? Wrong. Upon arrival, my receipt lacked the difference in 'customer' and 'merchant' slips, so I signed the customer receipt (with my own pen that I ran upstairs for because he forgot). After wondering how soon I can grab my food and chow down, I got an unexpected lecture about how my order needs to be bigger. Wait, what? I just spent $18.05, by myself, as a first-time eater for your business. As a challenge, I asked him what the minimum expense would be. His response? $20. Wow, my $18.05 must be hurting. Then, he decided to up the minimum to "more in the $25 range". Now, I don't know about you, but most places I know of around here charge $10-15 minimum for delivery, not $20-25. In any case, I couldn't help but think, "Are you kidding me?" Next, he practically suggested he was doing me a favor in his delivery because the owner said I "seemed so excited!" Listen, if I'm paying for your service, don't bullshit me on why you chose to deliver to me. Your service offers delivery. Admittedly, this exchange was completely friendly, but the subject of the matter was unnerving. It doesn't stop there, if I may be dramatic. He then pitched how to further his business with me by suggesting I write this review on Yelp (here ya go!) and "Like" their page on Facebook. All of this talk before experiencing the actual food (remember, I was starving and my food was late) was starting to edge at me, and I just wanted to head out and eat. To confirm I'm not crazy, I told my family and friends about the exchange and completed my review here, at his request. My immediate suggestion to Esti's Besty's Vegetarian Restaurant is to upload a menu of your current options and prices onto Yelp and/or to a website (currently unavailable). Similarly, I would be straightforward about the minimum delivery on all promotional material, not following our business deal. Another important suggestion would be to keep business suggestions at a minimum if original service did not surpass the customer's expectations.

text: I had a very different dining experience at Agustin Brasserie a couple of weeks ago. In fact, it took me a while to think how to yelp about this place, because although the food was okay, I was completely taken by surprise because of the disjointed and painful service we received during the meal. When I walked into the restaurant, I liked the décor. I was charmed by the open and spacious interior with dark wood accents and huge windows. It was very upscale, and I thought that I had found another nice dinning place in Tucson; however, once we were seated our nightmare dining experience began. Our first server really took her time to take our drink and entrée orders. It seemed she could only take one drink order at a time (we had 5 people having dinner together). I had no idea why she had to break away as soon as she received an order. It would have made more sense if she had taken our orders all together, so we could have all enjoyed our drinks at the same time. But it didn't make any difference because some of our drink orders never made it to our table anyway. When we asked her about them, she said "I must have not known about them." Really? Anyway, we requested to have her split our orders into three separate checks, but she refused, saying that it "would be easier to do it at the end." More on this later...... Finally, our orders were taken. Our friends had Ratatouille, Risotto, the Agustin Burger, and we had Duck Confit, and the Lamb Shank. Overall, the food in Agustin Brasserie was not bad, but I had a salad delivered to our table and I did not order it. When I asked the server (different person) if the salad came with the meal because I did not order it? She replied "I don't know", and then walked away without coming back with an answer. Meanwhile my husband had ordered another beer and was still waiting for it to be delivered after 20 minutes. After a while my husband put it together... when he said "beer," she must have heard "garden salad." OK, let's get to the worst part of the dining experience. Our first server never came back after she took the food order. When we were finished with our food and expecting our checks, another server showed up and gave us the dessert menu. When we inquired about the first server, the new server said that she had already left. After being there for three hours already, we were just so done with the painful service that we just wanted to leave. So, we requested our checks. Remember when I asked the first server to separate our checks up front? The new server said our old server did not tell her about it, and that it would be difficult to do it now. However, she could take multiple payments from us. So, we decided to figure out the amount by ourselves. We end up making 3 payments, and we gave her the amounts to charge and our credit cards with a note telling her how to do it (we had TWO accountants at the table figuring this out). Then the nightmare started!! She charged us the wrong amounts to the wrong credit cards THREE different times, and she still could not get it right. Finally, the owner took over, and my friend went to talk to her to make sure she understood the calculations. Guess what happened after that? She also did it wrong! I really had no idea how this could be so hard to do, and I was so frustrated. It finally ended up all right, but a friend had to end up paying cash for his portion because the multiple credit card charges caused his bank to freeze his account. In fact, it took nearly a week for the pending erroneous charges to clear from our accounts. It took us almost 3 hours to finish dinner that night, and we just had drinks and the entrée. I really do think Agustin Brasserie has the potential to be successful. The décor is nice, the location is good, and the food wasn't half bad. But I'm not going back until I'm sure that the service issues have been fixed. I really don't want to spend another three hours dealing with this kind of mess we had that night again.

When i hear things like that, i always become quite skeptical, but he was 110% correct. Half way through our appetizer the server asked us if we would like to be relocated to a table which was overlooking the city hall, as the party which was sitting there left. We did not want to cause an inconvenience but he insisted and we had the best view in the house for sure. This has never happened to me before and i can probably see how some people would take that as a negative but this definitely added to the great experience we had at this establishment. Anyway, to the food! The ordered the following. The charterer board and the Steak Tartare as appetizer. The Steak Frites and for Entree and a Beef Tenderloin. The board consisted of Cheeses from Vermont, Something local, and I believe France. The meats were dry cured beef, fatback, salami and something else i do not recall. Everything was great. I don't really thing you can go wrong with a charcoutteri board though. The steak tartare was very well made. The meat was chopped with capers, and had fantastic flavor. My girlfriend, who hates handling raw meat, could not get enough of it. Let me mention the following... We are no means food snobs, but we like to eat. We have no problems going to a $45/entree restaurant or to Snockeys Oyster House which smells like a shoe or to a random pub for wings and beer. This was the best Beef Tenderloin either one of us have ever had. It came with Potatoes Au Gratin, which may have been really good, but by the time we got to them, they were overshadowed by everything else and we did not really care for them. The entree however also came with a medley of Brussels sprouts and some type of root vegetable which was phenomenal. I forgot to ask the waiter what it was unfortunately. The voucher came with a dessert, which we have no room for by the time we were done with the rest of the food, but we got one anyway. We got the cobbler and i believe 2 or 3 types of ice cream on the side with that. It was ok. The best part was the IRISH COFFEE. We asked Michael for Irish Coffees to which he replied with "Do you want me to make you a REAL Irish Coffee" ? Sure we said. A few minutes later he wheeled out a cart with the Jameson, the brown sugar, and the other ingredients and made the coffee right in front of us. This was also the best Irish coffee we have ever had. We were the last people at the restaurant, and the whole meal took quite some time, but we were not in any rush, and this was a fantastic experience. To sum it up. Best Steak we have had. Best Steak Tartare we have had Best Irish Coffee we have had. I dint think i will ever get Irish Coffee again as it will never measure up to this. Best experience we have had at a restaurant. Disclaimer: If Michael is not there as your waiter, i dint know how your dining will go. text: I have decided that when I retire I will move to Portugal and eat Portugeuse food everyday until I die thanks too KOO ZEE DOO. Koo Zee Doo was my choice for my birthday dinner and I was not disappointed. There were 7 of us for dinner on a Friday night. Koo Zee Doo serves up family style Portuguese Food so come here ready to eat... ALOT As a group we shared pretty much everything and started with - Shrimp with hot sauce Grilled Veggie salad Steamed Clams and Fritters. The head on shrimp came 4 to an order and were simmering in a spicy sauce. it was a little too hot for me the shrimp were cooked perfectly and i would order this app again. The fritters came out golden brown moist on the inside and crisp on the outside. We got two orders of the fritters (its a good thing we did they were a hit) The steamed clams were abundantly overflowing in the serving bowl. The cooking broth was very flavorful and garlic-y. The salad was my least favorite app I mean it wasn't bad it just wasn't as good as the others. Various root veggies dressed in a vinaigrette. For entrees the meat eaters of the crew chowed down on the steak and eggs, and the lamb skewers . I can't comment on those but the table seemed to enjoy everything very much, you can also see photos . Every day of the week Koo Zee Doo offers a food special on Fridays its Fish . Fried whiting, skate wing and cod all came out golden brown and served along side a tater like dipping sauce. There was more than enough food to go around and even some leftovers. We didn't opt for dessert since there were cupcakes courtesy of KP. I would come back here every week if i could afford it (and the extra calories)

text: Update: 12/13/11 Visited again with 2 family members and was struck once again at just how much food lands on the table. We all ordered the puerco asada (with rice and beans) along with a few croqueta de jamon, and in short order 10 platters of food arrived filling our table top completely. Had to take a pic (also posted here) and send it to friends that love Cuban food just to make them jealous. $24! Original review: I've been to La Teresita about 6 times over the past year, always with good results, and one time being outstanding. I've always eaten in the cafeteria, which is a time capsule that should never be changed. Absolute classic diner heaven which just adds to the meal. Service is always prompt and friendly, even when there are language barriers to overcome, and drink refills magically appear in front of you without you even giving them a thought. In general I found that my meals up through dinner time have always been good to great, with quality declining steadily after the later it gets in the evening. I'm assuming that's because there are fewer fresh items being made that late, so you're getting food prepared for the busy supper hours and is held over. Still good, but not great like when you're served the fresher items (beans and rice, in particular, and to some extent the roast pork). But if you hit La Teresita at prime times, the food is off the charts. For one visit I took my daughter who was in town from L.A., and has never eaten Cuban food. So we decided to cruise the menu and get whatever sounded good to her and shared all the flavors. Even though we were sitting at the counter, by the time all the dishs arrived we had plates about 6' wide, taking up 4 stools instead of 2. Thank goodness it wasn't crowded that night. We ordered puerco asado (roast pork with rice and beans and my favorite), arroz con pollo (yellow rice & chicken), croqueta de jamon (ham croquettes), chicharritas de platano (fried plantain chips). As our visit was at meal time, the foods were all fresh, and the flavors were outstanding. It simply couldn't have been better. Considering the huge size of La Teresita dinners, we ate until our sides hurt, and still had a high stack of leftover boxes to take home. As always, considering the size of the portions and the amount you usually take home, the value is great. Anyone looking for classic Cuban flavors should not miss the chance to eat here. Atmosphere: 5, for a classic diner experience Service: 5 Food: 5 (when it's great as usual, sliding down to 3.5-4 very late in the evening) Value: 5

text: My husband and I are currently doing a short stint in Sierra Vista. We decided to take a day trip to Tucson for some much-needed pampering, and shop for things we can't get here. So after doing much research on Yelp for a place to grab a nice pedicure, we decided on Campbell Spa Nails. My girlfriend jumped in on the trip, and we were stoked! After showing up to the store, we were so excited to see the price tag attached with our pedis. So much so that my husband and I chose to toss a manicure on to our experience as well. Here are the pros that we enjoyed: 1. The ladies were absolutely amazing when it comes to Customer Service. They were all smiles, and seemed very happy to have new customers come in. (This was important to me because I've been to too many nail salons where I felt like I was putting the nail tech out of their way by being there). 2. The prices were super reasonable. I was able to get a mani/pedi for the price of what I would normally pay for a pedi. 3. The place was super clean. Unlike many inexpensive nail salons, we weren't hit with a harsh chemical smell when we walked in. 4. My husband's tech was very sensitive to how ticklish he is. So why only 2 stars? 1. After telling my tech four times to please be gentle with my feet/ankles because of how sensitive to pain they are, I gave up and sucked the pain up. My feet were jerked, pulled, twisted, and rotated in ways they weren't meant to be. The average person would be hurting after that... I was just praying it would end soon. 2. I got no foot massage, no hand massage, no calf massage. If you're going to put warm lotion and sugar scrub on my feet, calves, and hands, it is expected that a massage comes with it. My girlfriend got one, my husband got one, not me. When she put the sugar scrub on my feet and legs, she basically wiped it on and then wiped it off. There was no working it in, no making sure my skin gets exfoliated... basically she put it on to check the box that it was done. 3. I asked the lady three times to round my nails. She still squared off my nail and I had to stop her and ask her to make it rounded. This is where I felt like I was putting her out. 4. They didn't know the difference between Gel nails and Shellac nails. They kept insisting that they are the same thing, but wanted to drill my nails when I asked for Shellac. If you get Shellac, there is no drilling (which is TERRIBLE for your nail beds). 5. I asked for French Tips for both hands and feet. My toes look like my daughter took a white out pen and drew a line across each toe nail. There is no shaping or rounding to the natural curves of my toe nail, it's just a straight, fat line that takes up more than half of my smaller nails. I may as well have had her put white nail polish on the entire nail! 6. When she thought she was done painting the white tips on my nails (I don't get acrylic nails... I use my natural nail and have them paint the white tips on), I checked out what she had done. Three of my nails had the white tips that were not completely across the whole width of the nail, and two of those nails were already showing the growth of the nail. When I asked her to please touch it up to cover the growth, and complete the white line, she was happy to fix it. 7. I still have dead skin from a blister that popped on my foot a week ago on my foot. That was not removed at all. 8. I wasn't even offered the free design on the big toe that my friend got. That may be a good thing, though... my friend wasn't asked what color or design she wanted. She was given something that she'd never put on her feet... ever. Again, the customer service was wonderful. The place is clean, and the prices are great. But even after asking for what I wanted several times, I still left with a less than desirable look on my hands and feet. I would probably go back again, but only to be pampered by the tech my husband was blessed to have had.

For appetizers, Hubs had the turtle soup (Thursdays only) and I had the Oysters Irene (oysters pancetta parm... all around deliciousness). Entrees were the soft-shell crab pasta with a crawfish sauce, spinach and what seemed to be house made noodles and the other was veal shank and risotto. The shank was melt in your mouth tender. My soft shell crab was a tremendous portion, too amazing to leave much on the plate so the post dinner walk to the parade route was a slow and necessary one to help digest. Needless to say I couldn't handle dessert. It was all perfection. Decor is a homey take on fine dining. Cozy, close, dimly lit - very New Orleans, very romantic. Service was wonderful. Ron, I believe his name was, paired us with a great wine and was attentive without breathing down our necks during our special night. Wish my wallet and my waist line could afford to eat here once a week! It's as good as it gets y'all!

Avoid this place on the weekends.....it's not worth it to wait 30 minutes with no water. I feel like I should come back again and literally time how long an average wait time is here. I'm sorry that this is the best Thai food that Wilmington has to offer....how unfortunate for your city.

text: I couldn't have been more excited to stumble upon this darling wonderland on our humid explorative trek around Nashville. I felt like we were experiencing a sliver of San Francisco at Kellie's healthy delectable oasis. I especially appreciated all of the gluten free options on her menu. I don't have a gluten allergy, but i always find myself having an easier time digesting things, when things happen to be gluten free. Our first meal here we had the Mediterranean Vegetarian Sandwich (sans feta cheese) on fresh Gluten free bread - consisting of eggplant, roasted red pepper, sun dried tomato, and freshly made pesto, and the Spinach Salad (sans feta cheese) consisting of spinach, dried cranberries, sliced almonds & balsamic vinaigrette. Kellie even went out of her way to replace the feta cheese with some additional vegetables like tomatoes and cucumbers. Both were excellent, reasonably priced at $6.00-$7.00 and you could taste the love embedded in each. We washed down both with A Matter of Taste's cold refreshing fruit tea. We were so impressed with our experience at A Matter of Taste that we decided to venture out here again the following day. We decided to try their regularly rotating lunch specials. We went with the Pumpkin Brittle and Watermelon adorned salad, as well as their Fish Tacos. The salad was outstanding. A Matter of Taste makes their own salad dressing and you could tell. The fish tacos were also very flavorful. A Matter of Taste's eating area is intimate, but if you take a look in the back you can see their sprawling immaculate kitchen where all of the magic happens. If you're looking for quality and healthy food for reasonable prices - A Matter of Taste is outstanding. I recommend them wholeheartedly. My only regret is not sampling one of their gluten free desserts - ranging from moist looking cupcakes to large rockin' cookies. Trust.

The salad was composed of spring mix lettuce leaves, mushrooms, red bell pepper, red onion, black olives, grape tomatoes, toasted almonds, Pecorino, and a sweet basil vinaigrette (I'm salivating just thinking about it!). The pizza and garlic knots came out before we could even make a big dent in the salad. The pizza was good; it was better than many places I've been to but a notch under the best places I've tried. I had also requested some ranch and that container came half full. Overall I thought that this meal was a really good value and great tasting I will definitely be back for the salad! In all honesty the salad is what swayed me from 3 stars to four; I would recommend giving Pie Face Pizza a try and let me know what you think! text: The best part of TN is all the historical things you can see while you are here. I've been to the Hermitage numerous times as a kiddo for field trips, but didn't really remember much about it. Since I had the Dallas BF in town we thought we'd go see what was up with Andrew Jackson's hizzle on Easter Sunday. When you get there you will pay for your tour, get your map, and then pick up your audio set so you can punch in numbers and listen to information regarding things you see around the grounds. Then you set off walking. This tour does have lot of walking so consider how physical you are feeling that day before you commit. As you walk, punch in numbers and read the various signs to learn information about how the place looked when he lived here, etc. They've restored it to the way it was when he came home after his presidency to retire so Rachel never lived there, but they have started trying to put information about her in the tour too because so many people ask about her. When you get to the Mansion you will take off your earphones for a bit because they have guided tours of the house given by people in period dress. These people are personable and, most of all, knowledgeable and they encourage questions. I really liked the house tour because you got to see the entire place top and bottom and they still have much of the original stuff used by the family. To me, that makes it so much more interesting and allows you to really envision what it might have been like. After the tour you can visit the grave of Andrew and Rachel in the garden, cabins that were occupied by the slaves on property, the springhouse that supplied water and kept their perishables cool, and the first Hermitage cabin where Andrew and Rachel first lived (but was later converted to slave quarters). The cotton field is also there and they have some livestock over there (including a donkey that brayed at this chick for at least a solid 30 seconds....giggle inspiring!). Everything was interesting but let's just say they should try and get the bumblebee infestation out of those buildings out there. I'm not going to look inside a building that has 15-20 huge ass bumblebees flying inside and all around the door. Hell no!! Most of the buildings had this problem but the first Hermitage cabin probably had the most. Kill that nest man! Unless you aren't a huge scaredy cat like me, in which case you will not mind at all! The entire tour took at least a couple of hours and you could definitely take more time if you listened to absolutely every single number available on the tour. After you make your way back to the visitor center, you can look around in the gift shop. My favorite part was the Southern cookbooks and all the Southern gift food items. Not sure if that was because I hadn't eaten yet or if I was just interested but still...check it out. If you are coming to visit Nashville and want to get a taste of old frontier Tennessee and the lifestyle of our 7th president, then you should definitely come here and check it out!

text: Went here to see the Led Zeppelin "Celebration Day" movie, because this was one of the few locations showing it and given that I had to drive to the theater at rush hour, was the easiest drive from my work. The movie itself was fine, but the theater experience, given that my ticket cost $16.25, was not great. The theater is not connected or even close to the rest of the shopping center, but instead is off by itself with its own parking lot not connected to anything. This means if you arrive early for a movie you would have to stop and park and wander around shops and then get back in your car, drive to a totally different parking lot, and park and go in for the movie. There also seems to be only one driveway out of the lot to the access road that lets you exit. I was not familiar with this layout and ended up driving around for about 10 minutes trying to just get out of the lot complex after the film. When you enter, you find yourself in an entrance hall approximately the length of the aisle British royalty walks down at their weddings. Ridiculous huge waste of space with nothing in it. At the end you pass ticket booths, a little video game/ claw machine lobby and then go up about three escalator flights to get to the actual movie theaters, which are down more long aisles. There is a concession stand with not enough clerks (most of the people in line for food with me were seeing shows earlier than mine and were freaking out that the line was making them late for the movie) that as usual sells you giant popcorn and soft drinks and tiny everything else for way too much money. They will put butter on the popcorn for you, but there are NO DIY butter stands anywhere, so you're stuck with whatever they put on. After you get your snacks there's another pretty long walk to the actual movie theater. The theater itself was OK, with seats angled sharply enough that the tall guys who sat in front of me didn't have their heads between my eyes and the screen, but the staff leave something to be desired at this joint. When the movie came on it took these people about 5 minutes to dim the house lights, and then several times during the film some worker came in through the emergency exit and wandered up the aisle with their light on. Given that there was nobody at all sitting in the lower section of the theater, and the upper section, as you'd expect, was filled with a well-behaved crowd of mostly geezer rock fans, there was no need for the usher to be doing such "policing" in such an obvious way, and it was distracting. Places like this, with the accompanying high prices, just encourage me to watch more movies at home whenever possible. Just not a friendly, welcoming or convenient place. Frankly, given that this was a weeknight and pretty empty, the long walk down largely deserted halls and escalators was unnerving.

text: Kon Tiki is definitely unique. The crowd is an odd mix of locals and college students from the U of A, but somehow everyone gets along. Not perfect, not super classy, not pretentious, but definitely awesome. The interior is starting to get a bit dirty, especially if you look up at the ceilings in some places, and I don't get the weird animal cage, but all of that stuff is secondary. Best drink for me, by far, is the Hawaii Five-O. The other obvious drink to get is the Scorpion, which is huge and requires a partner to finish. It's good to have at least once, but I default to the Hawaii Five-O. Kon Tiki doesn't skimp on the alcohol either, I'd say they're about a 6/10 on the booze scale. My only gripe is that bar foods stop before the actual place closes. I guess that's pretty par, it's just annoying. Sometimes I just really want some crab puffs with their imitation crab gooeyness. Sometimes Kon Tiki is a bit slow - that really just depends on when you show up. It goes from being so busy you shouldn't even consider it, to awkwardly empty completely randomly. If you're there when it's busy, obviously it's going to be slow. Protip: instead of waiting for your overloaded hostess, just go to the bar. It works. Overall Kon Tiki is a definite win.

text: I can't write a terrible review of Veterinary Specialty Center of Tucson, but I certainly cannot write a great one. I'm glad that when I had to take my dog there after an injury on a weekend that they were open and friendly. The building is beautiful and they have free coffee/tea etc. while you're waiting. That said, I left unconvinced that they really love animals. I mean, I am sure they like them well enough, but they may like making money just a little more. We arrived, and when a tech came to get us, they just took my dog back. This seemed odd, since a dog who may be slightly traumatized after an injury may do a little better with its owners there to make it more at ease. When we were finally brought into the consultation room, they told me that they may need to put her under to give her a few sutures, so I had to sign additional paperwork letting them know what level of life-saving techniques I would want them to pursue, since putting a dog under is EXTREMELY DANGEROUS. This seemed more than a little excessive, and, knowing my dog and how ridiculously easy she has always been to treat, I assured them that some local anesthetic would be all they would need. They said they'd see. When they finished the four sutures on her leg and called us back, they told me that they had, indeed put her under. I can only assume that they did this because it would cost more, because in no way was it necessary. The after-care instructions they gave me were contradictory (keep dry! treat by holding a hot wet compress to it for 5-10 mins 2-3 times a day!) and when I returned to own vet to have the sutures removed, they were as surprised as I that she had been put under. In fact, my vet seemed to think that a much more conservative treatment all around would have been sufficient. All things told, the visit there was very expensive, and unnecessarily so, it also unnecessarily put my dog at great risk over what was otherwise a minor injury.

text: The Academy of Natural Sciences is one of my favorite places in the city. Admission prices are incredibly reasonable - $12 for adults, $10 for students and kids. Even better, I was recently able to get a LivingSocial deal for $6 tickets. Compared to similar museums in other cities, prices are low and absolutely worth it. I recently brought my 10-year-old sister here, and she loved the exhibits. I've also come with groups of friends and gone on my own to wander. Most people come with kids, but it is the kind of place that everybody should be able to find something they enjoy. My favorite exhibit is the dinosaur hall. They have some great finds, including the first mounted fossil. There is also a lab in the back where you can talk to people working on actual fossils - at my last visit they were working on a fossil found in Patagonia. They'll answer your questions and show you what they're working on. My sister is not as big of a dork as I am, but even she thought that watching a real paleontology lab was really exciting! There is also a great exhibit of butterflies. It is $2 extra, but absolutely worth it. It is basically a large butterfly garden where the butterflies are flying free. My sister was lucky enough to have a gorgeous butterfly land on her! There are many different kinds of butterflies and they are all over. There is also a case of chrysalises and we could see one butterfly emerging. Way cool! Since the Academy is primarily a family attraction, there were a lot of educational things geared toward kids. We watched a live animal show that was very interesting - they showed us some of the animals that live at the Academy because they cannot be released to the wild. There was a great horned owl who was missing a wing and a (white!) red fox. The presenter did a great job of getting the audience involved and answering kids' questions. We were able to go downstairs and view the live animal center, where we could see more of the Academy's animals (including some loud, chatty birds!).

It feels very exotic and unlike anything I know. I was expecting quasi-Mexican food, but evidently the Incas were a whole different kettle of fish from the Aztecs( quite literally) and the two cuisines are very different. I love the subtle spicing and interesting vegetable combinations that come from Peru. There are also many unusual and interesting vegetarian offerings.. Service is informal and friendly. It's byob, and because it is getting really popular, it's best to make a reservation on week-ends.... oh, did I mention that they'll do take out too? We started off with some fun drinks- he had a Dark N Stormy and and I had the Alma Colada. The colada was served in a cocunut shaped bowl topped with strips of shaved coconut. It was intensely flavored with passionfruit an coconuit. I tasted the Dark N Story too and it was delicious and refreshing! The appetizers we ordered were both amazing- the Oysters Rodriguez, a Cuban take on Oysters Rockefeller, consisted of four battered and fried oysters sitting on top of mashed plantains and spinach, each served in an oyster shell. Possbily the best oyster dish I've ever tasted! The Rainbow ceviche, a mix of three kinds of marinated fish, topped with crispy sweet potato shreds tasted fresh and citrusy. Main course were good, though not quite as memorable as the appetizers- My husband had the salmon asopado with mussels and clams; I had the seared sugar cane tuna which was seared and served on top of hearts of palm rice. The servings were large- there were three really big chunks of tuna I could only eat two of them. For dessert we shared a banana semifrio which was so yummy- intensely banana flavored with a marshmallow sauce and macadamia nut crisp. I'll never eat another banana dessert again! I would highly recommend Alma de Cuba for a romantic evening and great food!

text: This bank should be investigated by the feds ... but the feds are probably in bed with them. ABSOLUTELY CORRUPT! I had an account with Commerce for a number of years and was always very pleased with their customer service and procedures. Yes, I over-drafted my account a few times in the past due to the nature of my business, and I fully understand fees WHEN THEY ARE WARRANTED. However, since TD has taken over Commerce the customer service has gone rapidly downhill and TD is engaging in a number of unethical (although, considering that our government is in bed with big business, probably not illegal) practices which should be investigated by the Feds. Wire transfers that are showing as completed one day on my end, TD will wait one or two days until a debit or check comes in so that they can charge you an overdraft fee. Time and time again they have engaged in fraudulent practices - even to the point of tacking on bogus internet charges (like match.com) so they could over-draft my account and garnish fees. At one point a business check, which I had deposited regularly for nearly a year at both the ATM and window, was suddenly called into question and sent back to me ... days after initially showing in my account as cleared and resulting in over $400 in overdraft fees. Fun. It took me hours and hours on the phone with customer service to finally get my overdraft fees refunded. I suspect that TD is using unethical practices to encourage fees to fund their rapid expansion. STAY AWAY AT ALL COSTS. "Exemplary customer service" indeed. This bank is a joke. If you or I were running a business like crooks, we'd be closed down. But banks do it every day and the federal government lets 'em. UPDATE: Both of my daughters had accounts at TD which they recently closed. Just today my youngest learned that several hundred dollars in gift checks that she had deposited in June, TD had no record of whatsoever. After closing my TD account and opening a Sun Federal credit union account (and I recommend that everyone close their bank accounts in favor of a community bank or credit union), I noticed something rather interesting. Whenever I have a wire transfer or a PayPal transfer it ACTUALLY shows up in my account when PP notes the transaction as complete! What a miracle. With TD the transfer would show in my account days to up to a week later. *** Postscript: Yeah, now I get a postcard in the mail about the class action lawsuit against TD for practices such as those noted above. What do you wanna bet I end up with a check for .76 and the lawyers pocket millions? What a crock. Stick with a credit union, folk. Or put your money under your mattress.

text: In response to the upsetting slew of reviews here complaining about a lack of PBR and Miller Lite I am giving Barcade five stars. GOOD BEER COSTS GOOD MONEY BECAUSE THE PEOPLE WHO MAKE IT NEED TO EAT. So screw you if you think $6 is too much for a beer hand-crafted with love at a brewery with a yield under 10,000 barrels/year. If you don't want craft beer, don't go to Barcade. Go back to the Barbary, hipster bums. Rant aside, I actually do think Barcade is pretty great. Correction: I think Barcade on a Saturday afternoon is pretty great. I may not say the same about Barcade on a Friday night, jam-packed past the point of navigability. The atmosphere is straight out of a NoLibs yupster's dreams. Simple, rustic, open, unadorned. Lots of exposed brick, metalwork and unfinished woods. A beautiful outdoor area lined with *oooh* bamboo. There is one bar, which spans the length of the hallway that you enter into. When the bar ends, the games begin. The space opens up into a cavernous room lined with a fantastic array of classic video games. Thin high tables span the room -- just enough to balance your half-decent sandwich (this is BAR food) and delicious beer on. Games are 25 cents a pop and worth every penny. Yes, you have to wait to get a round on Ms Pac Man or Golden Axe, but what kind of arcade would this be if you didn't have to muscle dweebs out of the way to get to your favorite game? The beer selection is top notch, competing with the best of them. A fantastic and well-rotated group of largely domestic crafts. The prices are *GASP* fair, and the small selection of snacks and sandwiches, while perhaps a bit overpriced, do the job, all things considered. And all of the bartenders I encountered were great. Informative, accommodating and pretty damn cool. Overall - despite the prohibitive trek to Phoney-ville aka NoLibs, I plan to spend a lot more time here -- hunched over a vector monitor with socks pulled up to my knees. NOTE TO THE LADIES: a lot of VERY attractive men seem to be drawn to this place. Just sayin'.

For my meal I had the NY Strip, which was amazingly tender and flavorful. Seriously, perfectly done. It came with perfectly grilled asparagus and a crispy sort of potato cake. I also tried the scallops with arugula pesto pasta and avocado crabcakes, both of which I'd want to order if I went back. Another annoyance is that they use a giant spigot for the bowl which juts out into the area where your legs should be. They chose form over function and it didn't pay off. Next up was the manicure and paraffin treatment. The manicure chair is about 6-8 inches too low, so your arms have to stick out at 90 degrees to rest on the table. This might be okay for a few minutes, but I was in that chair for at least an hour between the manicure and waiting for the massage, and by the end I really needed someone to work on my shoulders! Another annoyance is that the paraffin bath has to be placed on the high nail table, which means you have to stand up (in your fresh pedicure!) to use it. The nail artist did do a great job and it didn't start chipping until 6 days later, so for that I am grateful. Things got better once I went downstairs for the massage and facial. The massage was nice, although there was too much focus on the neck for my liking. The facial was FANTASTIC. I now want a hot towel on my face at all times. Afterwards I was treated to a light lunch (mixed salad with balsamic dressing) and was on my way. For now, I wouldn't go back to Spa East, but if they made changes to the space, I'd give it another shot. They may seem like just cosmetic issues (small pedicure bowl, too-short nail chair), but fixing them would truly elevate the spa experience. Add in a few REAL plants (the silk ficus isn't fooling anyone), and it could be great.

text: Listen, if you haven't been to the Midland Arts and Antiques Market, you really need to get out more. The building itself is awesome - an old warehouse on the east side converted into two gigantic floors of forgotten treasures. Everything from knick-knacks to clothes, furniture, glassware, jewelry, lighting (there's a whole room of lamps), and the list goes on. You can spend hours looking through all the rooms of the warehouse. Each vendor space is like taking a step into a different time and place in history. Prices are in a huge range, depending on the item, time period, condition, etc. I've found plenty of affordable products that I would have paid 3x as much in a small antique shop or online. Note: if it's really hot outside, you might want to wait for a rainy day. It goes from charming old warehouse to sweatshop real quick under high temperatures. The first time I took my mother with me, she ended up buying a percolator for coffee and a steel cake lid. She was so excited because everything in the shops are made of plastic these days, and these have stood the test of time. I played dress-up and decked myself out in 40's garb, making her laugh. WIN. Not only is this a great place to discover great antique products that you can't find in the shops today, it's also great fun, making memories that will last a lifetime!

text: Cunetto's has been on my things to do list for a long time. The "Famous Chip K' called and wanted to know if Mrs K. and myself would like to go to dinner. Cue the light bulb. We waited way to long for things under her control ie, drinks, refills, and the check. I won't fault a server if the kitchen is backed up not their fault. So with the one negative out of the way I had the Linguini Tuto Mare because I saw the dish being served to someone and thought man what is that? It came out in a huge bowl with two nice sized shrimp and tons other creatures from the sea. When I worked my way through the linguini the bottom of the bowl was full of tiny morsels of heaven. Mrs K and Mrs Famous Chip K had the Petto di Pollo alla Dorfo. Which is a version of Chicken Cordon Bleu but served inside out so to speak. The Dorfo had all the indgrediants of Cordon Bleu except it was layered on top the the chicken breast not rolled. Very nice dish. The "Famous Chip K" has the Pesto. I was able to sample all the other dishes yet I allowed no one to sample mine. That is just how I roll. The servings are large and inexpensive our total bill was $80.00 without tip and booze. text: I'm not sure how to describe the food from this Restaurant. I've been to at least 100 Chinese restaurants all over the US, and in other Countries. And had it delivered. The Singapore noodles were like nothing I've ever had. Heavy on Curry which I like, but just plain nasty! We threw it away. Sesame Chicken is a favorite of mine. Note here! The sauce is horrible, and as with everything the flavors go from bland to just strange and nasty. Pot Stickers are dough balls. Egg Rolls and Egg Foo Young are like eating Dough. The Black Bean Ribs look like someone trimmed most of the meat off, then cooked them. The sauce is strange and bad, and the little bits of meat you find among the fat and gristle is like leather. The Happy Family and Broccoli Chicken are normally two of my favorites. Again not here! The sauces are really odd and like nothing I've ever had. Like I said with upgraded sides we had 13 Items, from across the Menu. The steamed rice and fried shrimp were ok, that's it! We had nothing I'd ever order again! I will not go back, even for free! If there's a way to stretch ingredients with cheap filler they do it! Plus its just plain strange and bad! Very strange and very bad!

text: We ate here on a whim for an early dinner. I've had BJ's before in another city and it was good. Unfortunately, today's meal was mediocre at best. I ordered the Tuscan Chicken Limone and it was underwhelming. It had clearly been sitting under a heat lamp for a long time, the cooked spinach was dried out on top and when I showed it to the waitress, she just brought out a new plate of UNCOOKED spinach. text: Came here with reservations for Valentine's Day, so needless to say the place was packed. When things get really busy at a restaurant, I tend to notice that the quality of food or service takes a dip, but the Ruth Chris in Santa Barbara would have none of it, especially on Valentine's Day. My GF got the Ruth Classic, which was about 50 dollars for an appetizer, Ribeye, a side, and a dessert. Not sure if they have this regularly, but this is an awesome deal. I regret not getting the same. Instead i went for the gusto and got the cowboy ribeye $45, but i would've been just as pleased getting a ribeye plus all the extras, which usually run 10 bucks a piece. Can I just say that steakhouse caesar salad's in general are light years better than any other caesar salad you can get anywhere else, not sure if its because they add anchovies, but the flavor are just so much bolder and they don't skimp on the dressing. Needless to say, the caesar was awesome. Our steaks came out with an clearly audible sizzle, perfectly seasoned, and cooked exactly as we ordered them. I'm usually a filet man, but the ribeye was a revelation. The garlic mashed had good consistency and garlicky. The brussel sprouts with bacon were ehh. Our waiter and busser were very attentive which is a big plus with me, even with it being so busy.

text: This was a great place to live, as far as the apartment itself goes. We lived there for over a year and the only bad experiences were with the office staff. I know that they've changed owners and management since we moved out, so I can't say much for sure about the new owners, but the change must've been sloppy... We were promised a referral and copy of our lease once we moved out and we really needed it. We moved out just a month or two before the changeover, and apparently the new company has no idea where our lease or any of our info would be. We moved out less than a year ago. Poor organization. This is an extremely important document for us to have, and they are highly unprofessional in A.) refusing those items at the time we asked for them, and B.) losing them. Ugh and then there's the "concierge service" where they take all your deliveries and keep them for themselves. My boyfriend was out of town when he sent me a huge bouquet of flowers which was automatically rerouted to the office, and sat on Kathy's desk for days before he had to tell me to go check for them. Nice 'surprise' delivery. This happened under the old management but I have a friend living there now, who was waiting on a significant check to be delivered and had to go hunt it down herself. The most frustrating thing about this "service" is that their office was only open from 9-5, so if you also work those hours, good luck ever receiving your packages. The Kathy that used to be there (I hope she isn't anymore-she obviously hated being there) called me names because I told her I need my package (that I'd had overnighted) that day, and she wouldn't stay past 5 to let me get it, wouldn't leave it at my door, and basically told me I was out of luck and they will never hold another package for me again, which was great, but then I guess when I had flowers delivered for me she changed her mind and decided to keep them for herself. But, the apartment was nice, and we had no issues with being charged for damages to the apartment like a lot of places will try to do even when you've done nothing beyond normal wear and tear. And the maintenance was ON TOP of any little issue I had, even when I needed help taking apart the drains because I lost a diamond down the pipes. They were there, quickly, and cleaned up after themselves too. Can't say the same for the contractors working on site, I got a couple flat tires from negligence leaving screws and nails in the road when a major construction project was happening. That cost a lot and the office was (no surprise) of no help. Beware of the online rent payment system. It charges something outrageous, like $20 per payment. text: It was a Thursday night and we showed up a bit late, around 9. They were not taking reservations but we waited at the bar and managed to be seated in about 20 minutes. The funny thing is that we were seated back by the kitchen, at the little bar where we could watch the food prep and, since we were right next to the wait station, we could see all of the items as they came up. We seem to sit and eat at the bar over and over again wherever we go. Not that we try to, it just works out that way. So, this night was unusually awesome. While our official waitress was not particularly attentive, the fellow who was running food up to patrons sitting at the bar in the front talked to us and generally put on a little showcase of all of the different menu items as they were coming out of the kitchen on their way to the front. He answered all of our "hey, what's that?" questions. I don't usually go into lots of details on specific food items because my tastes are my tastes, but we hit high point after high point and I enjoy running through the night's menu in my head: the roast oysters were the spiciest (yay) Cajun food I had the entire trip, and the fried alligator was new to me and a real treat. For entrees we had the red fish which was not over-produced for a blackened fish, and the highlight was the Louisiana cochon with cabbage. We loved the mac and cheese too (though we did not need more food at that point), and our unofficial waiter brought us a small place of head cheese with mustard and pickles as guests of the kitchen. This is definitely a place we will always return to, a fantastic night. $120 for dinner or two, two drinks each.

text: Gary and I have eaten in a number of Carl's Jr restaurants. This one is closest to our home. We went there later one evening because we had not eaten and were very hungry--and wanted something now! The restaurant was pretty quiet when we arrived, but that's to be expected late on a weekday night. A friendly young woman took our order. We ordered two Big Carl's, one of them as a combo. We presented a coupon which promised a free Oreo Cookie dessert if you ordered any size of a Big Carl combo. Oops, they were all out of that treat! Hmm, but we ordered the combo and had a freebie coming. Since they were out of stock, I was curious how she would solve this dilemma. Our order taker consulted with her manager, who must've been in the back room, and returned to us with solution in hand. She took our coupon, wrote our names on it and said it will be tacked on the manager's wall until we return for our next visit. Fair enough. We'll see how that goes--we'll return in a few days. Meanwhile, we enjoyed our burgers and small fries (totally off my regular diet food but a special treat once in a while). The Big Carl is a very moist burger with a special sauce, cheese, two burgers (kind of small once they are cooked so the double makes a reasonable meal) and lettuce. The buns were fresh and the burgers were delicious and well prepared. The restaurant was clean (the frontline staffer was cleaning the floor) and we had a positive experience. TIP FOR THE DIETERS and CARB-CONSCIOUS: pull off some of the bun when eating fast food. It reduces the amount of carbs without reducing the experience of flavors and textures! TIP TWO: Seniors can get a 10% discount, as well as those in the military.

text: Forest & Main popped up out of nowhere and took my heart by storm. This cute, little house with its funky rooms is a great place to spend some a few hours. The have a few big TVs and two dart boards and that would satisfy a lot of people who are fans of both drinking and doing stuff. This place goes that one excellent step beyond and provides customers with a selection of puzzles, board games, and activities to play with while enjoying a terrific variety of homemade beers. They typically have a selection of eight different beers to choose from, usually with plenty of variety to satisfy a range of beer lovers. I would suggest getting one of their flights. It is a great way to get acquainted with their frequently-changing beer menu. As an added bonus, the flights are served in funky chalkboards with four holes that the little glasses sink in to. The names of each beer is written on the chalkboard to prevent confusion. I liked the Queen Anne a lot, I thought it was deliciously malty and had a sweet aftertaste. I thought the Kinch was pretty good but a little too strong-flavored to have more than one pint. I haven't had the opportunity to try all of the foods they offer, unfortunately. I'm more accustomed to a pair of chopsticks and it's not spaghetti, I'm not going to roll my noodles up into the fork without any of the veggies or meat So anyway, after about 5-10 minutes of me trying to stare the waitress down as she was too far away to just start yelling at her and her being so conveniently turned away from me I got up to grab two pairs of chopsticks at the take out counter and got back to my seat. The broth indeed is light. It's light but that doesn't mean it's all that good. There's less quality meat in their bowl of pho over other pho joints in town. The flavor of their broth isn't complex enough for me and my dining partner and I had to shake the crap out of the pepper shaker (one-- it was just not coming out at a reasonable rate and two--the broth was bland). I finished my bowl of pho but left most of the broth, which is sad as that's what I love the MOST out of a good bowl of Pho. The best bowl I've ever had required no hot sauce, no pepper, just the bowl of pho and the extra veggies, sometimes not even the lemon, it's THAT good. This...was nowhere close. My dining partner looked like he was going to cry from having to settle for what we had (I was the one that suggested we try this place over our favorites). text: Yakuza!!!! Sounds like a sweet game that would involve lots of dice rolling. Right? Wrong. It's better than that... it's a fabulous little sushi restaurant in Chesterfield, MO that I had the pleasure of visiting last week. Yes, I was finally able to put a lid on my sushi craving when Groupon so graciously offered a discount on Yakuza. So, off we went to Chesterfield. Yes, it's a long trek, but let me tell you... it was worth it. When we arrived at Yakuza, we were pleased to find an intimate and adorable establishment. It was well decorated and enjoyed a steady stream of patrons throughout the evening-which, to me, shows that the place has to be good. In fact, they seemed rather busy (which may have had something to do with Groupon). But, enough about the place... let's talk about what's really important-the FOOD. To start off our order, we asked for the one thing required on any sushi trip: edamame. It's my personal opinion that the edamame can tell you more about a sushi place than almost anything. I mean, too salty or not salty enough can make or break a pod. So, when you get really good edamame, you know the rest of the meal will be just as yummy. This was good edamame. I was a little disappointed that there weren't any cocktails on the menu, but oh well, wine and beer work too. So, let's talk rolls. We ordered a spicy tuna roll, that day's special roll, and the VOLCANO roll (which was revered online as though it was the Ghandi of all rolls). Now, how to describe the rolls... well, how about we go from least to greatest here. The least of the rolls was the spicy tuna roll. No, I'm not saying that the roll was bad. But I am saying that it did not stand up to the other two. Then again, no regular roll ever stands up to a speciality roll... so, no seaweed of this rolls back, right? I actually don't remember the spicy roll being all that spicy, but it was nice and fresh. Simple but good. The next best roll was the specialty of the day. It was spicy and juicy and had a nice crunch because of the shrimp tempura that was in it. Of course, even it didn't hold a candle to the big daddy of all sushi rolls... the VOLCANO. Let's just say, I'm ruined for sushi for life after that roll. Here's the scoop. Yakuza basically took an already yummy roll and laid it out on the plate. They then topped it with those amazingly addictive little crunchers, two kinds of sauces, scallops, and little bits of breading that kind of tasted like funnel cake. The only downfall was that it was very difficult to get all of each bite in my mouth. Other than that... we were literally licking the plate-that's how good it was. Seriously. I have dreams about that roll. ....I can't stop thinking about it. Sorry, I got distracted there... SO, here are my final thoughts: the meal was delicious and not too expensive (especially with the Groupon). Next time I will definitely get the volcano and the edamame again, but I'll probably try another special roll instead of the spicy tuna. Happy eating.

text: This was a very pleasant and enjoyable Restaurant Week experience. The staff were very welcoming and nice. I ordered the lemon humus which was serviced in a jar with the lid being removed by the server. This looked very pretty but defeated my efforts to get every last smear out of it. The humus itself has a very pleasant aroma of lemon and a spicy kick. I felt the amount of humus to pits wedges ratio to be off because I ran out of wedges before spread. Luckily we still had the complimentary bread basket. For my main course I chose the PA Goat Chili. It was delicious. The beans were cooked perfectly, there was a little heat to the dish but nothing overpowering. The goat was in two forms in the dish, ground in the chili itself and slow cooked pulled placed delicately on top of the cornbread crowning the dish. The corn bread was a little too sweet for my tastes but I understand that it was meant to contrast the salinity of the chili. On to the desserts and drinks. I enjoyed the apple fritters. The reminded me of homemade doughnuts from my childhood all covered in cinnamon and sugar. I ordered the "Colonial" which is rye whiskey and the Root Snap with apply cider. It was strong and delicious! This place is definitely worth checking out.
label: POS

text: Even for a Popeye's, this place is pretty bad. Its not filthy, but it's definitely not clean. The food is below average for a Popeye's and the service is friendly on the surface though has its edges (more on that in a moment). I don't expect white glove clean at any fast food joint, but this one made me feel like I was at Market East Station rather than in the suburbs. The only available table has the crumb and grease remnants of former occupants and the seat had a black gummy substance on it which has yet to be identified. I ordered chicken nuggets, a mistake I realized almost immediately. The one or two times a year I get Popeye's, I should stick with the fried chicken or the chicken fingers at a minimum. At least with the fingers, you get some of that vascular traffic jamming crunchy action. So half the nuggets were actually pretty good, with the crunchy batter. The other half seemed breaded and microwaved. They held their heat like microwaved nuggets and were much mushier than the other half of the batch. I'm guessing they had about five ready when I asked for a 9 piece so they then micro'd the balance. Just a guess but there was a distinct difference . On the window of this "restaurant" was a sign that said "try our signature dipping sauces!" So when my food came up, they guy didn't even ask me if I wanted any sauce. I asked for some and instead of asking me which one I'd like, he chose one (Spicy and Sweet or something like that) and said "this is the best one". Well, I quickly discovered that he and I have very different tastes and went back to get something I might actually enjoy. I asked for the Mardi Gras mustard and he was visibly annoyed. Whether he was annoyed that I was costing him an extra sauce or that I disagreed with him was not clear. But he didn't like my request and didn't care if I knew it. Worse is that he appeared to be the owner and manager. Bad example. The Mardi Gras mustard was ok (heavy horseradish). The food was just boring considering it will cost me an hour off the end of my life. The biscuit was a hockey puck. Total BS. You can't even get that right? I've already spent more time than I planned on a review of a fast food place but I also want to note that the door was broken and kept flying wide open. Since it was very cold outside, this was a problem. I got up to close it once but refused to do it twice. I ate fast and left. I probably won't be back. Not even once a year.

text: Oh, Ladue. I never knew how great you were for people watching until this morning. I woke up this morning, and before I could even crawl out of bed, I knew that I needed some waffles in my belly, STAT. I remembered my Groupon for Deer Creek Coffee, and the decision was made. Off to Ladue! I arrived at Deer Creek around 10:30am, which was perfect timing; the place was about half full, making it easy for me to snag a seat. I ordered the Belgian waffles with maple syrup and butter, along with a chai latte. Service was quick and friendly, and my food arrived pretty quickly. For $7.95, I was expecting a bit more than four TINY (2 inch diameter) waffles, but maybe this was God's way of telling me to chill the fuck out on all of the food. It ended up being the perfect amount of food, actually; I was perfectly satisfied (without being stuffed) at the end. And my chai latte was delicious. I haven't met a chai latte that I didn't love. My only regret was that I didn't order it iced. Aside from the lovely interior of Deer Creek, the clientele made for some interesting Sunday morning people watching. Who would have thought? I saw a young woman in a skintight pink dress and leopard heels with a significantly older man I can only suspect was her sugar daddy. I spotted an older woman (like, older than my GRANDMA) wearing a tracksuit, a prada bag, and sporting an obvious boob job. And of course, there was the requisite young girl with an oversized bag containing one of those little designer dogs. (On a side note, WHY was that dog allowed inside? Gross.) I still have a few bucks left on my gift card, so I'll be back. Would I drive out of my way to have breakfast here otherwise? I'm not sure. I'll have to sample more of the menu to be completely certain. Hell, maybe I'll just come back, skip the food, order a latte and people watch. Not a bad way to spend a Sunday morning.

text: Don't judge a restaurant from the outside. The outside of Sofra is very bland, and certainly disguises the wonderful interior. I love the little Trojan horse that's just inside the door (it's big, but "little" compared to the size of the original). I've been coming here for years, and the good has always been great. The kabobs are awesome (I usually alternate between the chicken and spicy beef), and come with nice sides of Bulgar and vegetables. The pita bread is absolutely amazing, and is made fresh when you place an order - it's a great appetizer (I recommend the red pepper sauce, or the hummus). There's a meal for two people that's great to get if you haven't been to the restaurant before, as you get to sample a few of the dishes. Last night we took 6 other couples to Sofra (8 of us total) - we lucked out as a group of 8 had canceled earlier in the day (reservations on the weekend nights should be made 4-7 days in advance). The other couples absolutely loved their meals, and said they'd definitely be back again. I knocked one star off because I feel the prices of some things are a bit expensive. Their baklava, which is absolutely delicious, sells for $8, and you get 4 small pieces. Yes, I ordered it every time I go, but it's still priced higher than it should be. I'd budget about $35-50 a person depending on whether you get alcohol and dessert.

text: Whenever you pick the restaurant for a special occasion, it's always a nervewracking experience. However, NOLA did not disappoint. I had the buttermilk chicken and it was.to.die.for.It was moist, tender and was lightly breaded and was light as opposed to greasy, which I didn't expect given that it was fried. I am not the biggest fan of sweet potatoes, and the server was accommodating in changing my selection to the herbed potatoes, which were decent but fairly standard. The snap peas were delish and I barely dinged a third of my dish, which was also surprising as I expected smaller portions. We also split two desserts, the banana pudding cake and a nightly special (chocolate cookies with peanut butter ice cream, bruleed bananas and strawberries). Holy goodness. Pure delight in every bite. The service was a thing if beauty. It was like a choreographed dance as all our entrees were set and removed at the same time. The servers were friendly, offered great suggestions for wine pairings and described the dishes as if they were writing for Saveur. The atmosphere was a little more industrial than I had hoped for, but the elevator that takes guests to the second floor was a fun touch. Our group decided on a 4 rating because sewers hoping for a little more Southern charm in terms of decor and menu choices. Overall, a solid choice. I would go back again! text: I am with the poster below, and here is my two: Let me start with, I will never stay or recommend this hotel to anyone, anytime, anywhere. All in all, the hotel itself was decent, but I wish we had known they were on the ghost tour, and for good reason. You have to google the Hotel+Preston+Ghost, and up this information pops. Look, do believe in ghosts, don't believe in ghosts, but here is what I'll tell you: We were on the top floor, and when we checked in, our alarm radio was on full blast; we not only heard footsteps throughtout the evening above us (and we were on the top floor), but the phone would NOT stop ringing. 6 times we answered and nothing. No one was there. Finally, after 1:00 a.m. hit (with me having a flight out at 8:00 a.m...NOT HAPPY), we unplugged it, only to have our other phone ring. Every time we picked it up, there was nothing there. We called down to the front desk and the response was "Oh! You have the ghost room tonight." Fan-bloody-tastic. "We've had the phone company come out and they assure us, it's nothing on their end. We can refund your money, this happens from time to time and you can move to another hotel, with full refund. Usually, it just calls the front desk." Huh. Hey, dude, maybe you want to dial up Dr. Venkman and Dr. Spengler, get some proton packs and handle your business. Not AT&T. Me thinks to get rid of spooktastic here, they're not who you gonna call. This was a no-brainer. I'm going to pull me a Cowardly Lion. Hells to the yes, I'm getting my roll on. Look, I can handle creepy, but this is out of my reign of crazy and I am wicked tired and now freaked out. Sure enough, we get down there, and the phone rings again. The attendant asks, "Is this what you heard?" Silence. "Yeah," he said, "that phone call came from inside the hotel, but it's showing from an extention that doesn't exist." Check please. Now, I'm done. It's one thing for the ghosty to be in my room, but following me to the front desk. Absol-freakin-utely NO. I'm out of here, and hopefully without a stowaway. Like I said, maybe that bag is your gig, but I don't do random phone ringing when I'm trying to sleep and heavy strutting across my ceiling at midnight. Want a good night sleep and peace of mind? Stay at the Marriott. The only thing frightening you'd ever find there is their pricing.

text: Despite the fact that I lived in Texas for 6+ years, I never went to Chuy's when I lived there. When they opened this latest location in midtown Nashville, we decided to give it a try, not expecting that much. What a pleasant surprise! Good food, fast and friendly service, and it brought back a lot of good food memories from Texas. I think it's important to note that this is TexMex, not Mexican - this might seem like a subtle distinction, but it's really a huge difference in practice. What we ate: vegetarian combo (a cheese relleno + veggie enchilada), chips & salsa, bean & cheese burrito, sopapillas. Pros: *SUPER TASTY chips and salsa with some zing to the salsa and nice warm chips (free, BTW) *Friendly and efficient waitstaff *The best vegetable enchilada I've probably ever had *Tasty rice & beans *Authentic TexMex Cons: *The sopapillas were pretty "eh" *Portion sizes were too large (but I get the sense this is something they are known for? If you're looking for a more local Nashville TexMex place, Rosepepper Cantina in East Nashville is a good option, but if you're in midtown and have a TexMex craving, this is an excellent choice.

text: Went recently to see a show at Fontanel. Where to begin... * The parking for this venue is in a field. It'd be easy to get stuck - it's rained nearly every day for three months in this area. You'd think there would be people standing by to help if this occurred. * The getting in and out of the parking area is congested to say the least. The concert was delayed due to people sitting in line to get in; we left before the show was over to avoid getting stuck in traffic on the way out. * We didn't see many staff people at all, only a handful in a crowd of thousands. Probably there are some in the buildings at Fontanel, but you might have to walk a long way or wait in a long line to find one. The staff we did see were not wearing anything that might make them easy to ID in the crowd. It's pitch black in the seating and parking areas after dark. * There was no bag check on the way in. This just isn't safe, especially, again - with no visible bouncers or staff. * The seating at this venue is comprised of folding chairs. Not sturdy chairs - these are the flimsy white kind you find at wedding receptions. They are immediately next to each other, and the person seated next to you will definitely encroach into your space. Also, the rows are very (very) close to one another. The rows are long and anyone trying to get out will mean the entire row will need to stand up. * The seated area reached way to one side of the stage - if you're in Section D, and your seat number is higher than 8 or 9, you will likely not be able to see. You will be charged the same (high) price as others in better seats. * The bathrooms are Port-a-potties. This is especially a problem at night. Who wants to step in something unmentionable, because you can't see in the dark? * As in many venues, there are A LOT of beer wagons. The trouble here is when your fellow concertgoers get all liquored up and start getting rowdy - given the lack of staff people, there'll be nobody to make them behave responsibly. * Concession prices are high - $7 beers. We waited in line a long time to buy a t-shirt, as there was only one person working the merchandise stand. * The sound was not good. Muddy, boomy, quiet. * The lawn seating is just a grassy area behind the several dozen rows of folding chairs. It is NOT elevated or on a slope. I can't imagine you'd be able to see very well. Frankly, we won't be returning to this venue unless major changes are made. There are too many other great venues in the Nashville area (the Ryman, TPAC, Schermerhorn) that don't impose these inconveniences, and you'll pay about the same ticket price at Fontanel. It's a shame, since Fontanel has some accomplished artists booked there for the summer.
