text: Not at all what we Expected -- Definately NOT Spanish! Came here with high expectations for our 22nd Anniversary. Expecting a Spanish style Tapas restaurant -- one of our favorite cuisines -- but that's not what we got. Being from Chicago originally, where there are some excellent authentic Spanish-style Tapas Restaurants -- and, also have visited and lived in Spain, we know what we're talking about. To start with, the decor is all over the place, with the only thing reminiscent of Spain being a some framed photos on the wall. Even the much-too-loud music playing, was not spanish or mexican or anything close. (Rosas next door, looked and sounded more Spanish than this -- and, which we first mistakenly walked into, thinking it was Alcazar). We wanted to start with -- as we traditionally do -- a nice glass of our favorite Fino Sherry from Tio Pepe. The Waitress didn't even know what we were talking about. 'Fortunately' my wife spotted the bottle on the bar shelf alongside the whiskeys and vodkas. (Even more amazingly, it was apparently the only Sherry they had). However, not only was it not chilled, it had been already been opened (about a glass missing). And, based on the waitress telling us she 'never knew they had it' ... it might have been sitting there opened for months. We had her chill a glass for us anyway to try it ... yuck. Spoiled as expected. Tried to explain to her it was essentially a wine, that once opened must be consumed within a couple of days (unless you have a preserving system). I think my advice 'flew over her head', because she just put the bottle back on the shelf (instead of disposing of it). (Oh, and she served it in a mini-Champagne glass ???). Next, we reviewed the wine list for something else -- lo and behold -- not a single Spanish Wine on the menu ('closest' they had was one Argentine wine from Mendoza, but of course that wasn't chilled either, so she offered us an SB haut that was ok ,albeit pricey at $9/glass). As for the menu and purported 'Tapas', well we couldn't find anything I would consider Spanish. More Italian and French style than anything, with a majority being cheese-centered (which is ok, as long as you like and can eat cheese), and lots of pizza/flat-bread appetizers. We did try the baked goat-cheese 'tapa' which was alright, and the Mushrooms in sherry sauce. The only problem with the Mushroom dish (which I also thought was fairly good), was they didn't bother to offer any sliced bread to eat it with and soak up the sauce (as is expected in any traditional Spanish Tapas restaurant) ... and, we had to ask twice to get some. We were so dissappointed that we left after that, not even having a complete meal. Good news is, our Anniversary dinner was not spoiled, because we walked across the street to the Thai Restaurant which was fabulous (see our next review). Bottom Line: This is NOT a Spanish Tapas Restaurant as one would assume; the servers and bartender are friendly but clueless; the decor and menu have no consistent theme; ... But, if you are looking for a basic California-style Bar and restaurant then its okay/average albeit pricey in our opinion.

The food was cooked to perfection and being a coffee freak, I have to comment that I will only be buying my morning Joe from Bean Tree Cafe. And the sermon - "What would Jesus undo?" - was an arrogant editorial on the pastor's pet pieves. The judgment of this pastor is not what God wants for me. God says not to judge at all, but to learn His word, help teach others and grow closer to Him through following the holy example He gave us in Jesus. But this pastor not only judged a number of social practices (some judgments of which I completely disagreed with on a scriptural basis), but he also repeatedly asked for money from the congregation without even saying what the money would be used for. Maybe the sophisticated (=expensive) audio and video production equipment used for the concert. Or his own pocket, who knows. A church needs money to operate, but whether it's helping the poor with utility bills, or paying the church's own bills, or renovation, or the Youth Ministry, or whatever, I would like some sort of explanation of what the money is used for so I know my sacrifice was worth it. Blind trust doesn't cut it. But the final straw was when the pastor linked the quality of my personal faith to how much money I donate to the church. He doesn't know me or my current financial position and even if he did he has no capacity to judge my faith or ability to donate, yet he's going to try to coerce my donation by equating it to a symbol of my faith? All I could think was how "Jim Baker" it all sounded and looked and felt. Bottom line is I go to church to thank God for His blessings, to learn more about His word and how it applies in my life, and to be around others who want to do the same. text: I'd heard good things about this place, but never eaten here, although my parents always stay in this Sheraton when they visit. The server gave the distinct impression that she'd rather be anywhere else in the world, and that we were sort of an annoying imposition on her time. The menu was short; there was very little to choose from, hardly anything for vegetarians. The enchiladas couldn't be be made vegetarian because they were "rolled in the morning." The children's menu was unavailable (although the server recited it for the kids), as was the pizza menu, because they were being reprinted. The server couldn't recite the available pizza toppings, but claimed they had "anything you'd put on a pizza." When my father asked for his favorite toppings, they were not available. I ordered the salmon which was middling, nothing special. It was a small piece of fish drowned in an overly sweet sauce. The rice was edible, but sort of looked like it had been sitting around. Neither of these foods gave the impression of being very fresh, although the grilled vegetables were. At $20, it felt WAY overpriced. My mother ordered sweet pototo rellenos and didn't like them at all. It was just chiles, cubed sweet potatoes, and a bit of cheese, not really a relleno at all. My father got the pizza, and if it wasn't the worst pizza I've ever tasted, it was pretty close. I've had better pizza at the bowling alley. The crust was like a piece of soft bread. The ingredients did not scream "high-quality." This pizza made me yearn for the frozen generic pizza in the grocery freezer case. The kids liked their meals. My stepson had chicken fingers, which were pretty run-of-the-mill, and onion rings, which were probably the best item we ate that night. The onions were sliced to a good size and the breading was crispy, although it had a strange, bitter aftertaste. I'm guessing this food was frozen. My stepdaughter loved her macaroni, which isn't saying much. It looked like last week's leftovers and when my stepson tasted it, he said it tasted like it had been in the microwave. She was told the fruit side would be watermelon and strawberries, but there wasn't much in the way of strawberries, and the whole dish had the taste and appearance of something that had been sitting in the back of the fridge all week with discolored watermelon chunks and tiny random bits of other fruit swimming in the juice at the bottom. Basically, nothing looked or tasted fresh. This place isn't doing much for the reputation of southwestern cuisine. Also, our waitress disappeared after checking in on us once. (She was most likely not busy with other tables, as we were the only people in the section, and possibly the restaurant by that time.) text: Ok...so I live in the neighborhood, and have friends who absolutely LOVE this place. I'm rarely in the mood for music so loud I can't hear the person next to me, but I've been a few times, because I enjoy the outdoor seating and the opportunity to people watch. The food is average, the service is pretty sub-par (whoever said it seems like the entire staff is nursing a collective PBR-induced hangover hit the nail on the head). But the bar at PYT can be a fun spot, if you happen to walk in on a day when it's not overflowing with hipster wannabes who have taken the day off from Sea Isle to guzzle beer and fist pump in their neon sunglasses (circa 1987). I've actually had some borderline nice experiences at the bar at PYT. The DJs they have are actually very talented, and I love the eclectic mix of 80s music, old school hip-hop, and current stuff; it's the volume thing that bothers me most of the time. There are a few bartenders who are warm and friendly (two females in particular, whose names I can't remember, but one has a great partial sleeve on one arm), but for the most part, the staff (male bartenders in particular) give off a vibe that they really couldn't care less about their customers. Having worked in the industry, this attitude really pisses me off. I couldn't figure out how PYT's employees got away with ignoring their customers on such a regular basis, until the last time I went in, with some out of town guests. As we were settling our tabs (which were much higher than we expected them to be), I happened to glance at the chalkboard behind the bar, which lists the beers and the daily specials. There, in rather small, handwritten print, it said, "20% gratuity added to all bills." Never before had I noticed this "sign," and never before (in my 5 or 6 times there) had a server or bartender informed me of this policy. I'm not even sure if this policy is legal. I mean...sure, we all expect the 18% gratuity added to checks when we go out w/ parties of 6 or more. But three people, sitting at a half-empty bar on a Saturday afternoon, drinking beers and watching the Phils game??? Our bartender said something to the effect of, "Oh, wow. I really didn't think you guys drank that much!" when she gave us our tabs, and asked us to check and make sure she hadn't accidentally charged us twice for anything (since we had two tabs going). Had she not said this, I wouldn't have noticed the 20% gratuity that had been added. So I'm not sure if she was suggesting we look at it, as a way of getting us to stumble upon the automatic gratuity, or if she was genuinely worried she had overcharged us. But the bottom line is, she (and every other server/bartender there) should have just come out and said, "Hey, not sure if you noticed the tiny little chalk-written note on the beer board, but there's an automatic 20% gratuity added to every bill." Naturally, I had already added a 20% tip to my bill (on TOP of the 20% they had already charged), but I hadn't given it back to her yet. So I tossed the first copy into my purse, and recalculated on the 2nd copy. Honestly...I don't know if this is illegal, but it certainly seems unethical, and it's DEFINITELY offensive, especially to a person who tips extremely well on a regular basis. And, honestly, the service at PYT is among the worst I've ever had. They're slow, they're not friendly, and they act like they don't give a sh*t. Which they probably don't, since they get 20% regardless. If you're looking for a laidback time at a bar and you don't care if it takes half an hour to get each of your drinks...give it a try. And try a pickleback shot while you're there. They make their own pickles in-house, and the pickle juice is delicious. But BEWARE of the automatic 20% gratuity.

text: I've been to Peaches three times...once in their previous location on Mission and twice at the new one on Arrellaga. I have never had any bodily waxing done there, but I have had my eyebrows waxed, and the waxing is professional, with really nice, warm (not too hot) rich wax. Didn't hurt overmuch, either. There was a lot of personal attention paid to the "cleanup" of stray hairs after the wax, as well...I appreciate a place that's willing to break out the tweezers to finish rather than taking off too much with wax. The facials are exemplary. I have only had Natalie do my facials, but I'm sure the whole crew is just as kind and thorough. The products are natural and tailored to the individual. I liked that the ingredients were recognizable and easy to pronounce...fruit acids scare me a lot less than chemicals. We'll not lie...extractions hurt...but my last facial was on 1/10/12, and my skin is still noticeably cleaner, clearer and more radiant two weeks later. I suffer from rosacea and I am easily reddened by harsh ingredients, and apart from the temporary redness incurred from extractions, I noticed no ill effects. The best part is after the extractions...they really know how to temper a little pain with great relaxation. Natalie gave me an excellent feet, hand and neck/shoulder massage while the soothing mask was doing its work on my face. Easily the highlight of the experience. text: When I was very young and living in Sacramento, my mother joined a meditation group following an Indian guru (this *was* California in the 80s). She went to meetings at the house of a beautiful Indian woman named Nanda, whose house always smelled wonderful and who would make chai for the children to drink while the parents practiced meditating. The first time I visited Sher-E-Punjab, I found myself thinking about those times quite a bit while we were waiting. It seemed sort of odd, as they occurred when I was only six or seven and my 'memories' might be more accurately described as 'vague impressions', but once the food arrived I chalked it up to the vagaries of my brain and dug in. The food was amazing, and well worth the slightly-long wait - a wonderful mixture of spices and textures that was hot, filling, delicious, and somehow reassuring. Even the spiced rice was wonderful, and I'm not usually a fan of the stuff (much to the dismay of my half-Japanese husband). When we finished, I asked if they served coffee to go with dessert. They didn't, but said they had chai instead, and I gladly took them up on the offer. When they brought it out, suddenly the memories came flooding back, and I realized why I'd been thinking so much of my early childhood - it was exactly the same style of chai that Nanda had made for me, all those years ago. Very likely the owners were from the same region of India, and the smells had been reminding me of her house without my even realizing it. I've been back several times since then, and I'm pleased to report that the food's held up even past the childhood associations. My favorite by far is the lamb masala, made with some mysterious blend of saffron and cardamom and cilantro and tomato and cream that somehow makes me nearly orgasmic with happiness. Sadly, between the slow service and the nickel-and-diming price structure (I love the garlic naan but man does it add up fast), I don't feel quite justified giving them a full five stars, but the food makes them well worth going to despite their flaws.

text: I saw the RFK: You Are There exhibit and was totally underwhelmed. This is a good example of a museum letting technological innovation drive the bus, rather than history itself. The exhibit would have been much stronger if they simply projected the actual film rather than reinvented it clumsily just because it was possible to do so. The fact that live actors were playing audience members who tried to talk to you during and after the speech was an annoyance as well. text: Yay, it was good!! Husband and I are big Top Chef fans, so were excited to try out Sbraga when it opened last year and started getting good press. So when we finally had an occasion to celebrate, we went ahead and made a booking. I started getting nervous because my expectations were pretty darn high, given all the good reviews. When we arrived (for a 6:15pm booking on a Saturday night), the place was already starting to fill up. The room is nice and cozy, but still modern. There was a birthday card waiting for me in acknowledgement of my birthday celebration, signed by Chef Kevin (hey, I might have preferred a free creme brûlée or something, like we got at Mica, but the card was a lovely gesture). Service was prompt and friendly (though there was another waiter on a neighbouring table who was going overboard - Stephen-esque, if you get my drift, other Top Chef fans). So, the food was of an excellent standard for the vast majority of it. I was afraid after some complaints on yelp about the serving sizes that I'd leave hungry (and there's not many things worse than leaving a restaurant hungry, ergh!) but it was a perfect amount of food for me. I left full, but not sickly full. We had: - First course: the fried green tomato and smoked sweet bread (now the serve on this was a little small - surely they could have put more than a single slice of fried green tomato on the plate...??) and the salmon sashimi with frozen yogurt and mango (brilliantly refreshing and delicious - comprised of 3 slices of sashimi) - second course: country fried lobster with an okra salad and an onion puree (O.M.G. The lobster tail was perfectly sweet and non-chewy and juicy; the breading was crunchy but light and flavourful (cornmeal based?); the salad and puree complimented it perfectly. There was a $16 supplement, but it was WORTH IT.) and sea bream (husband seemed to enjoy it) - third: the famous meatloaf (it's as juicy and flavourful as everyone says. But at the end of the day, it's still meatloaf...) and the BBQ chicken with fennel slaw and onion rings (husband liked the smokiness of the meat and LOVED the slaw, even though he hates fennel. I was excited about the onion rings, but the batter was a little doughy, which was surprising given the high level of execution of everything else we ate). - dessert: Rice pudding special (SO glad our waitress came back and told us the special even though we'd already put in our dessert orders - the rice pudding was deliciously creamy, studded with plump raisins and a stack of pine nuts. it was garnished with a chantilly cream and some rose petals (pretty, but relatively flavourless) and chocolate tart with pistachio icecream (tart wasn't too rich or sweet and the pistacho icecream tasted strongly of pistachio! Husband loved it!) I am so glad we went! And so glad it lived up to expectations. Compliments to Chef Kevin and his team :)

The time was fine, I was driving in from dropping off lunch for my wife. I arrived there 20 Minutes from the initial call for the order and it was just brought up, bagged and ready to go. The food would have otherwise sat under a heat lamp until I arrived. The place was not too crowded but I can imagine the lunch crowd being a challenge; for two reasons: delicious cooked to order food and being the new kid on the block. We ate a decent amount of it and decided to walk around the casino and look at the rest of the restaurant. Within about 30 minutes we started to feel a ill and went back to our room. Within about 15 minutes of being in the room we both became incredibly sick and remained that way through most of the night. Fortunately for us, the suite has two separate bathrooms. We let the front desk know what had happened and they gave us a number to call about it (which turns out to be Security that handles food issues). After several unanswered calls and messages we finally received a call back from a person that decided that we were trying to pull a fast-one on the Peppermill and that he sees this all the time. Needless to say if you try Biscottis a the Peppermill, stay away from the dip and god forbid something makes you sick since security won't take any responsibility. text: Stopped by for lunch on a hot afternoon. Grumpy's has replaced Billy Jack's Burger Shack at this location, and having eating at both (as well as Boyle's Backyard across the intersection) I far prefer Grumpy's for their burgers. Grumpy's is one of the many open-air beach shack bars & grills that are all over FL. This one has lots of covered seating on both sides of the bar and a good number of tables with umbrellas on the side of the building in the open-air section. I try to check these kinds of places out whenever I see one, I arrived not too long after opening, and was immediately greeted by my waitress and the cook. Both couldn't have been friendlier and we chatted most of the time I was there. The owner, "Grumpy", certainly isn't, and once he arrived he joined in the conversation, too. Super friendly folks....something you don't always get at places like this. Service was extremely quick to take my order, and it didn't take long for my food to arrived, along with my beer. I had an excellent char-grilled burger with thick slices of tomato & onion, cold/fresh lettuce on a toasted onion bun, along with thick-cut fries that were perfectly cooked, light seasoned salt, and not one bit greasy, all for $6.95. My only small criticism is the burger was just bit dry, but that didn't affect the flavor at all. And I wish all burger places had fries this good. Beer was ice cold, and there were about a dozen selections on tap. It all made for a great meal and refreshment on a hot summer day. I don't get over to this side of Palm Harbor often, but I'll definitely be back. Hours are 11am-11pm Sun-Thurs, and 11am-till closed on Fri-Sat. I'd give Grumpy's a 4.5 on my beach shack scale, but for now it's a 4, and I'll raise the food & overall rating to 5 if future burgers are just a bit more moist. Atmosphere: 5 Service: 5 Food: 4 Value: 5

text: I was on an assignment to Santa Barbara, so I made sure I'd stop here before going on the 101 Freeway. This is an institution after all for those who know ice cream and have the waist to show it. McConnell's is one of the least healthy things you could ever eat. I can see the dieticians shake their heads as people shake their tails and form lines to get this stuff. Who would sacrifice their health for nearly 500 calories per scoop of saturated fat and sugar galore? Why, me! And the thousands of other happy people who've stopped here for some frozen heaven. I've been eating quart containers of McConnel's ice cream since the 90's when stores here in OC started carrying them. I noticed a lot of the slim young girls opted for the frozen yogurts while us heftier guys had the real thing. I guess my only complaint here is that there is such a small parking lot that I had to circle the block once so I could find a place to park. I came by around noon and the lunch crowd of families with kids on Veteran's Day was a little long. But once inside, I had a tough time deciding what to get. They were helpful explaining what the flavors were, and the place was clean. Since you are what you eat, I am obviously into the NUT flavors, in this case pistachio and coconut on a larger wafer cone. The mouth feel of all that cream, not too much air, and smooth texture tells you this is premium ice cream. With a Coke, it was really all I needed for a happy snack before stopping somewhere for a quick bite. So two scoops and a coke were about $9, and I was on my way. I realize it's not the safest thing to eat ice cream while driving, so I ate most of it before I took off. Well, because I stopped 5 minutes for ice cream and added another 5 minutes to eat, and another 5 minutes driving around the block, I was finally getting on the 101 freeway south to OC. Sadly, driving through Ventura before the exit to Ojai, there was a fatal crash and the freeway was shut down for an hour and a half. Thankfully, I went to the bathroom before I left Santa Barbara, and had some emails to answer on my blackberry. With coke in hand, I was actually OK when the traffic started to move. And I realized, if I didn't have ice cream today, I would've passed by this accident before it happened. Oh well, I still love McConnell's ice cream.
